59_3_17: But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, willing to yield, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, without hypocrisy.
59_3_18: And the seed whose fruit is righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.
59_4_1: What is the source of quarrels and of conflicts among you? Is it not this — that your pleasures wage war within your members?
59_4_2: You lust and do not have, so you murder. You are envious and cannot obtain, so you fight and quarrel. You do not have, because you do not ask.
59_4_3: You ask and do not receive, because you ask with wrong motives — so that you may spend it on your pleasures.
59_4_4: You adulteresses, do you not know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? Therefore whoever wishes to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God.
59_4_5: Or do you think that the Scripture speaks in vain: "He jealously desires the Spirit which He has made to dwell in us"?
59_4_6: But He gives a greater grace. Therefore it says, "God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble."
59_4_7: Submit therefore to God. Resist the devil — and he will flee from you.
59_4_8: Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners — and purify your hearts, you double-minded.
59_4_9: Be miserable and mourn and weep. Let your laughter be turned into mourning, and your joy to gloom.
59_4_10: Humble yourselves in the presence of the Lord, and He will exalt you.
59_4_11: Do not speak against one another, brothers. The one who speaks against a brother, or judges his brother, speaks against the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but a judge of it.
59_4_12: There is only one Lawgiver and Judge — the One who is able to save and to destroy. But who are you, who judges your neighbor?
59_4_13: Come now, you who say, "Today or tomorrow we will go into such and such a city, and spend a year there, and engage in business and make a profit" —
59_4_14: yet you do not know what your life will be like tomorrow. You are just a vapor that appears for a little while, and then vanishes away.
59_4_15: Instead, you ought to say, "If the Lord wills, we will live and also do this or that."
59_4_16: But as it is, you boast in your arrogance. All such boasting is evil.
59_4_17: Therefore, to one who knows the right thing to do, and does not do it — to him it is sin.
59_5_1: Come now, you rich — weep and howl over your miseries which are coming upon you.
59_5_2: Your riches have rotted, and your garments have become moth-eaten.
59_5_3: Your gold and your silver have rusted; and their rust will be a witness against you, and will consume your flesh like fire. You have stored up your treasure in the last days!
59_5_4: Behold, the pay of the laborers who mowed your fields — and which has been withheld by you — cries out against you. And the cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of hosts.
59_5_5: You have lived luxuriously on the earth, and led a life of wanton pleasure. You have fattened your hearts in a day of slaughter.
59_5_6: You have condemned and put to death the righteous one — he does not resist you.
59_5_7: Therefore be patient, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the farmer waits for the precious produce of the soil — being patient about it, until it gets the early and the late rains.
59_5_8: You too be patient. Strengthen your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is near.
59_5_9: Do not complain, brothers, against one another — so that you yourselves may not be judged. Behold, the Judge is standing right at the door.
59_5_10: As an example, brothers, of suffering and patience, take the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.
59_5_11: Behold, we count those blessed who have endured. You have heard of the endurance of Job, and have seen the outcome of the Lord's dealings — that the Lord is full of compassion and is merciful.
59_5_12: But above all, my brothers, do not swear — neither by heaven, nor by earth, nor by any other oath. But let your yes be yes, and your no, no — so that you may not fall under judgment.
59_5_13: Is anyone among you suffering? Let him pray. Is anyone cheerful? Let him sing praises.
59_5_14: Is anyone among you sick? Let him call for the elders of the church, and let them pray over him — anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord.
59_5_15: And the prayer of faith will save the one who is sick — and the Lord will raise him up. And if he has committed sins, they will be forgiven him.
59_5_16: Therefore, confess your sins to one another, and pray for one another, so that you may be healed. The effective prayer of a righteous man can accomplish much.
59_5_17: Elijah was a man with a nature like ours — and he prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the earth for three years and six months.
59_5_18: And he prayed again, and the sky poured rain — and the earth produced its fruit.
59_5_19: My brothers, if any among you strays from the truth, and one turns him back —
59_5_20: let him know that he who turns a sinner from the error of his way will save his soul from death, and will cover a multitude of sins.
54_1_1: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the command of God our Savior, and of Christ Jesus our hope —
54_1_2: to Timothy, my true child in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
54_1_3: As I urged you when I was leaving for Macedonia — remain in Ephesus, so that you may instruct certain men not to teach a different doctrine,
54_1_4: nor to give attention to myths and endless genealogies, which give rise to mere speculations rather than the stewardship from God which is by faith.
54_1_5: But the goal of our instruction is love — out of a pure heart, and a good conscience, and a sincere faith.
54_1_6: Some have wandered away from these things, and have turned aside to fruitless discussion —
54_1_7: wanting to be teachers of the Law, even though they do not understand either what they are saying, or the matters about which they make confident assertions.
54_1_8: But we know that the Law is good, if anyone uses it lawfully —
54_1_9: knowing this: that the Law is not made for a righteous man, but for those who are lawless and rebellious, for the ungodly and sinners, for the unholy and profane, for those who kill their fathers or mothers, for murderers,
54_1_10: for the sexually immoral, for those who practice homosexuality, for kidnappers, for liars, for perjurers, and whatever else is contrary to sound teaching —
54_1_11: according to the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, with which I have been entrusted.
54_1_12: I thank Him who has strengthened me — Christ Jesus our Lord — because He considered me faithful, putting me into service,
54_1_13: even though I was formerly a blasphemer and a persecutor and a violent aggressor. Yet I was shown mercy, because I had acted ignorantly in unbelief.
54_1_14: And the grace of our Lord overflowed for me — with the faith and love which are in Christ Jesus.
54_1_15: This saying is faithful and worthy of full acceptance: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners — of whom I am foremost.
54_1_16: Yet for this reason I was shown mercy: so that in me, the foremost, Jesus Christ might display His perfect patience as an example to those who would believe in Him for eternal life.
54_1_17: Now to the King eternal — immortal, invisible, the only God — be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
54_1_18: This charge I entrust to you, Timothy my child — in accordance with the prophecies previously made concerning you — that by them you may fight the good fight,
54_1_19: keeping faith and a good conscience. Some have rejected these and have suffered shipwreck in regard to their faith.
54_1_20: Among these are Hymenaeus and Alexander — whom I have handed over to Satan, so that they will be taught not to blaspheme.
54_2_1: First of all, then, I urge that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made on behalf of all people —
54_2_2: for kings and all who are in authority — so that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and dignity.
54_2_3: This is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Savior,
54_2_4: who desires all people to be saved, and to come to the full knowledge of the truth.
54_2_5: For there is one God — and one mediator also between God and men: the man Christ Jesus,
54_2_6: who gave Himself as a ransom for all — the testimony given at the proper time.
54_2_7: For this purpose I was appointed a herald and an apostle — I am telling the truth, I am not lying — a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
54_2_8: Therefore I want the men in every place to pray, lifting up holy hands — without anger and disputing.
54_2_9: Likewise, I want women to adorn themselves with proper clothing, modestly and discreetly — not with braided hair, and gold, or pearls, or costly garments,
54_2_10: but rather, by means of good works, as is fitting for women making a claim to godliness.
54_2_11: Let a woman quietly receive instruction with full submissiveness.
54_2_12: But I do not allow a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man — but to remain quiet.
54_2_13: For it was Adam who was first formed, and then Eve.
54_2_14: And it was not Adam who was deceived, but the woman, being deceived, fell into transgression.
54_2_15: But women will be preserved through the bearing of children — if they continue in faith and love and sanctity, with self-restraint.
54_3_1: This saying is faithful: if any man aspires to the office of overseer, it is a fine work he desires to do.
54_3_2: An overseer, then, must be above reproach — the husband of one wife, sober-minded, prudent, respectable, hospitable, able to teach,
54_3_3: not addicted to wine, not violent — but gentle, not quarrelsome, not loving money;
54_3_4: managing his own household well — keeping his children under control with all dignity
54_3_5: (for if a man does not know how to manage his own household, how will he take care of the church of God?);
54_3_6: and not a new convert — so that he will not become conceited and fall into the condemnation incurred by the devil.
54_3_7: And he must have a good reputation with those outside the church — so that he will not fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.
54_3_8: Deacons likewise must be men of dignity — not double-tongued, or addicted to much wine, or fond of dishonest gain;
54_3_9: but holding the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience.
54_3_10: And these too should first be tested — then let them serve as deacons, if they are beyond reproach.
54_3_11: Women must likewise be dignified, not malicious gossips, but sober-minded — faithful in all things.
54_3_12: Deacons must be husbands of only one wife — managing their children and their own households well.
54_3_13: For those who have served well as deacons obtain for themselves a high standing — and great confidence in the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
54_3_14: I am writing these things to you — hoping to come to you before long.
54_3_15: But in case I am delayed, I write so that you will know how one ought to conduct himself in the household of God — which is the church of the living God, the pillar and support of the truth.
54_3_16: And by common confession, great is the mystery of godliness: He who was revealed in the flesh, was vindicated in the Spirit, was seen by angels, was proclaimed among the nations, was believed on in the world, was taken up in glory.
54_4_1: But the Spirit explicitly says that in later times some will fall away from the faith — paying attention to deceitful spirits and to doctrines of demons,
54_4_2: by means of the hypocrisy of liars seared in their own conscience as with a branding iron,
54_4_3: men who forbid marriage, and who advocate abstaining from foods which God has created to be gratefully shared in by those who believe and know the truth.
54_4_4: For everything created by God is good — and nothing is to be rejected, if it is received with gratitude;
54_4_5: for it is sanctified by means of the word of God and prayer.
54_4_6: In pointing out these things to the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus — constantly nourished on the words of the faith and of the sound doctrine which you have been following.
54_4_7: But have nothing to do with worldly fables fit only for old women. On the other hand, train yourself for the purpose of godliness.
54_4_8: For bodily training is of little profit — but godliness is profitable for all things, since it holds promise for the present life and also for the life to come.
54_4_9: This saying is faithful and worthy of full acceptance.
54_4_10: For it is for this we labor and strive — because we have set our hope on the living God, who is the Savior of all men, especially of believers.
54_4_12: Let no one look down on your youthfulness — but rather, in speech, conduct, love, faith, and purity, show yourself an example of those who believe.
54_4_13: Until I come, give your attention to the public reading, to exhortation, and to teaching.
54_4_14: Do not neglect the spiritual gift within you — which was given to you through prophecy with the laying on of hands by the council of elders.
54_4_15: Take pains with these things — be absorbed in them, so that your progress will be evident to all.
54_4_16: Pay close attention to yourself and to your teaching. Persevere in these things — for as you do this, you will save both yourself and those who hear you.
54_5_1: Do not sharply rebuke an older man — but rather appeal to him as a father; and to the younger men, as brothers;
54_5_2: the older women, as mothers; the younger women, as sisters — in all purity.
54_5_3: Honor widows who are widows indeed.
54_5_4: But if any widow has children or grandchildren, let them first learn to practice piety in regard to their own family — and to make some return to their parents. For this is acceptable in the sight of God.
54_5_5: Now she who is truly a widow — and who has been left alone — has fixed her hope on God, and continues in supplications and prayers night and day.
54_5_6: But she who lives in indulgent pleasure is dead, even while she lives.
54_5_7: Prescribe these things as well, so that they may be above reproach.
54_5_8: But if anyone does not provide for his own — and especially for those of his household — he has denied the faith, and is worse than an unbeliever.
54_5_9: Let a widow be enrolled who is not less than sixty years old — having been the wife of one man,
54_5_10: having a reputation for good works: if she has brought up children, if she has shown hospitality to strangers, if she has washed the saints' feet, if she has assisted those in distress, and if she has devoted herself to every good work.
54_5_11: But refuse to enroll younger widows — for when they feel sensual desires in disregard of Christ, they want to get married,
54_5_12: thus incurring condemnation, because they have set aside their previous pledge.
54_5_13: And at the same time they also learn to be idle — going from house to house. And not merely idle, but also gossips and busybodies, talking about things they ought not to mention.
54_5_14: Therefore, I want younger widows to get married, bear children, keep house, and give the enemy no occasion for reproach.
54_5_15: For some have already turned aside to follow Satan.
54_5_16: If any believing woman has dependent widows, she must assist them — and the church must not be burdened, so that it may assist those who are widows indeed.
54_5_17: The elders who rule well are to be considered worthy of double honor — especially those who work hard at preaching and teaching.
54_5_18: For the Scripture says, "You shall not muzzle the ox while it is threshing," and, "The laborer is worthy of his wages."
54_5_19: Do not receive an accusation against an elder, except on the basis of two or three witnesses.
54_5_20: Those who continue in sin, rebuke in the presence of all — so that the rest also may be fearful of sinning.
54_5_21: I solemnly charge you in the presence of God and of Christ Jesus and of His chosen angels — to maintain these principles without bias, doing nothing in a spirit of partiality.
54_5_22: Do not lay hands upon anyone too hastily — and do not share responsibility for the sins of others. Keep yourself pure.
54_5_23: No longer drink water exclusively, but use a little wine for the sake of your stomach and your frequent ailments.
54_5_24: The sins of some men are quite evident, going before them to judgment. For others, their sins follow after.
54_5_25: Likewise also, deeds that are good are quite evident — and those which are otherwise cannot be concealed.
54_6_1: All who are under the yoke as slaves are to regard their own masters as worthy of all honor — so that the name of God and our doctrine will not be spoken against.
54_6_2: Those who have believers as their masters must not be disrespectful to them because they are brothers — but they must serve them all the more, because those who partake of the benefit are believers and beloved. Teach and preach these principles.
54_6_3: If anyone advocates a different doctrine, and does not agree with sound words — those of our Lord Jesus Christ — and with the doctrine conforming to godliness,
54_6_4: he is conceited, and understands nothing. But he has a sick craving for controversial questions and disputes about words — out of which arise envy, strife, abusive language, evil suspicions,
54_6_5: and constant friction between men of depraved mind and deprived of the truth — who suppose that godliness is a means of gain.
54_6_6: But godliness, with contentment, is great gain.
54_6_7: For we have brought nothing into the world — and we cannot take anything out of it either.
54_6_8: And if we have food and covering, with these we shall be content.
54_6_9: But those who want to get rich fall into temptation and a snare, and many foolish and harmful desires — which plunge men into ruin and destruction.
54_6_10: For the love of money is a root of all sorts of evil — and some, by longing for it, have wandered away from the faith and pierced themselves with many griefs.
54_6_11: But you, O man of God — flee from these things, and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance, and gentleness.
54_6_12: Fight the good fight of faith. Take hold of the eternal life to which you were called — and for which you made the good confession in the presence of many witnesses.
54_6_13: I charge you in the presence of God — who gives life to all things — and of Christ Jesus, who testified the good confession before Pontius Pilate,
54_6_14: that you keep the commandment without stain or reproach until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ —
54_6_15: which He will bring about at the proper time. He is the blessed and only Sovereign — the King of kings and Lord of lords —
54_6_16: who alone has immortality — dwelling in unapproachable light, whom no man has seen or can see. To Him be honor and eternal dominion. Amen.
54_6_17: Instruct those who are rich in this present world not to be conceited, or to fix their hope on the uncertainty of riches — but on God, who richly supplies us with all things to enjoy.
54_6_18: Instruct them to do good, to be rich in good works, to be generous and ready to share —
54_6_19: storing up for themselves the treasure of a good foundation for the future — so that they may take hold of that which is life indeed.
54_6_20: O Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you — avoiding worldly and empty chatter, and the opposing arguments of what is falsely called knowledge.
54_6_21: Some have professed it, and have gone astray from the faith. Grace be with you.
48_1_1: Paul, an apostle — not from men nor through any man, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised Him from the dead —
48_1_2: and all the brothers who are with me, to the churches of Galatia:
48_1_3: Grace to you, and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ —
48_1_4: who gave Himself for our sins, so that He might rescue us from this present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father —
48_1_5: to whom be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
48_1_6: I am amazed that you are so quickly deserting Him who called you by the grace of Christ — for a different gospel,
48_1_7: which is really not another. There are some who are disturbing you, and want to distort the gospel of Christ.
48_1_8: But even if we, or an angel from heaven, should preach to you a gospel contrary to what we have preached to you — let him be accursed!
48_1_9: As we have said before, so I now say again: if anyone is preaching to you a gospel contrary to what you received — let him be accursed!
48_1_10: For am I now seeking the favor of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? If I were still trying to please men, I would not be a bondservant of Christ.
48_1_11: I would have you know, brothers, that the gospel which was preached by me is not according to man.
48_1_12: For I neither received it from man, nor was I taught it — but it came through a revelation of Jesus Christ.
48_1_13: For you have heard of my former manner of life in Judaism — how I used to persecute the church of God beyond measure, and tried to destroy it.
48_1_14: And I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries among my countrymen — being more extremely zealous for my ancestral traditions.
48_1_15: But when God — who had set me apart from my mother's womb, and called me through His grace — was pleased
48_1_16: to reveal His Son in me, so that I might preach Him among the Gentiles, I did not immediately consult with flesh and blood —
48_1_17: nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me. But I went away to Arabia, and returned once more to Damascus.
48_1_18: Then three years later I went up to Jerusalem to become acquainted with Cephas — and I stayed with him fifteen days.
48_1_19: But I did not see any of the other apostles — except James, the Lord's brother.
48_1_20: (In what I am writing to you, behold — before God, I am not lying.)
48_1_21: Then I went into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
48_1_22: I was still unknown by sight to the churches of Judea which were in Christ.
48_1_23: But only — they kept hearing, "He who once persecuted us is now preaching the faith which he once tried to destroy."
48_1_24: And they were glorifying God because of me.
48_2_1: Then after fourteen years, I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus along also.
48_2_2: And I went up because of a revelation. And I submitted to them the gospel which I preach among the Gentiles — but I did so in private to those who were of reputation, for fear that I might be running, or had run, in vain.
48_2_3: But not even Titus, who was with me, was compelled to be circumcised — though he was a Greek.
48_2_4: But it was because of the false brothers who had been secretly brought in — who had sneaked in to spy on our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, in order to bring us into bondage.
48_2_5: We did not yield in submission to them, even for an hour — so that the truth of the gospel would remain with you.
48_2_6: But from those who were of high reputation (what they were makes no difference to me — God shows no partiality) — those of reputation contributed nothing to me.
48_2_7: But on the contrary — seeing that I had been entrusted with the gospel to the uncircumcised, just as Peter had been to the circumcised
48_2_8: (for He who effectively worked for Peter in his apostleship to the circumcised, also worked effectively for me to the Gentiles),
48_2_9: and recognizing the grace that had been given to me — James and Cephas and John, who were considered to be pillars, gave to Barnabas and me the right hand of fellowship — that we might go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcised.
48_2_10: Only they asked us to remember the poor — the very thing I also was eager to do.
48_2_11: But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face — because he stood condemned.
48_2_12: For prior to the coming of certain men from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles. But when they came, he began to withdraw and hold himself aloof — fearing the party of the circumcision.
48_2_13: And the rest of the Jews joined him in hypocrisy — so that even Barnabas was carried away by their hypocrisy.
48_2_14: But when I saw that they were not straightforward about the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in front of them all: "If you, being a Jew, live like the Gentiles, and not like the Jews — how is it that you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?"
48_2_15: We are Jews by nature, and not sinners from among the Gentiles —
48_2_16: knowing that a man is not justified by works of the Law, but through faith in Jesus Christ. Even we have believed in Christ Jesus — so that we may be justified by faith in Christ, and not by works of the Law. For by works of the Law no flesh will be justified.
48_2_17: But if, while seeking to be justified in Christ, we ourselves have also been found sinners — is Christ then a minister of sin? Absolutely not!
48_2_18: For if I rebuild what I once destroyed, I prove myself to be a transgressor.
48_2_19: For through the Law I died to the Law — so that I might live to God.
48_2_20: I have been crucified with Christ. And it is no longer I who live — but Christ lives in me. And the life which I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God — who loved me and gave Himself up for me.
48_2_21: I do not nullify the grace of God — for if righteousness comes through the Law, then Christ died for nothing.
48_3_1: You foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you — before whose eyes Jesus Christ was publicly portrayed as crucified?
48_3_2: This is the only thing I want to find out from you: did you receive the Spirit by the works of the Law, or by hearing with faith?
48_3_3: Are you so foolish? Having begun by the Spirit, are you now being perfected by the flesh?
48_3_4: Did you suffer so many things in vain — if indeed it was in vain?
48_3_5: So then, does He who supplies you with the Spirit and works miracles among you, do it by the works of the Law, or by hearing with faith?
48_3_6: Just as Abraham believed God — and it was reckoned to him as righteousness.
48_3_7: Therefore, recognize this: that those who are of faith are sons of Abraham.
48_3_8: And the Scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, preached the gospel beforehand to Abraham, saying, "All the nations will be blessed in you."
48_3_9: So then, those who are of faith are blessed with Abraham, the believer.
48_3_10: For all who are of the works of the Law are under a curse — for it is written, "Cursed is everyone who does not abide by all things written in the book of the Law, to perform them."
48_3_11: Now that no one is justified by the Law before God is evident — for, "The righteous one shall live by faith."
48_3_12: And the Law is not of faith. Rather, "The one who does these things will live by them."
48_3_13: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the Law — having become a curse for us. For it is written, "Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree" —
48_3_14: so that in Christ Jesus the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles, and that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.
48_3_15: Brothers, I speak in human terms: even with a man's covenant, when it has been ratified, no one sets it aside or adds conditions to it.
48_3_16: Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his Seed. He does not say, "And to seeds," as referring to many — but rather to one: "And to your Seed," who is Christ.
48_3_17: What I am saying is this: the Law, which came four hundred and thirty years later, does not invalidate a covenant previously ratified by God — so as to nullify the promise.
48_3_18: For if the inheritance is based on the Law, it is no longer based on a promise — but God has granted it to Abraham by means of a promise.
48_3_19: Why the Law then? It was added because of transgressions — until the Seed should come, to whom the promise had been made — and it was ordained through angels by the agency of a mediator.
48_3_20: Now a mediator is not for one party only — whereas God is one.
48_3_21: Is the Law then contrary to the promises of God? Absolutely not! For if a law had been given which was able to impart life, then righteousness would indeed have been based on law.
48_3_22: But the Scripture has shut up everyone under sin — so that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe.
48_3_23: But before faith came, we were kept in custody under the Law — being shut up to the faith which was later to be revealed.
48_3_24: Therefore the Law has become our tutor to lead us to Christ — so that we may be justified by faith.
48_3_25: But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a tutor.
48_3_26: For you are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus.
48_3_27: For all of you who were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.
48_3_28: There is neither Jew nor Greek; there is neither slave nor free; there is neither male nor female — for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
48_3_29: And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's offspring — heirs according to promise.
48_4_1: Now I say, as long as the heir is a child, he does not differ at all from a slave — although he is owner of everything,
48_4_2: but he is under guardians and managers until the date set by the father.
48_4_3: So we also, when we were children, were held in bondage under the elementary principles of the world.
48_4_4: But when the fullness of the time came, God sent forth His Son — born of a woman, born under the Law,
48_4_5: in order that He might redeem those who were under the Law — that we might receive the adoption as sons.
48_4_6: And because you are sons, God has sent forth the Spirit of His Son into our hearts — crying out, "Abba! Father!"
48_4_7: Therefore you are no longer a slave, but a son. And if a son, then an heir through God.
48_4_8: However at that time — when you did not know God — you were slaves to those which by nature are no gods.
48_4_9: But now that you have come to know God — or rather, to be known by God — how is it that you turn back again to the weak and worthless elementary principles, to which you desire to be enslaved all over again?
48_4_10: You observe days and months and seasons and years.
48_4_11: I fear for you — that perhaps I have labored over you in vain.
48_4_12: I beg of you, brothers, become as I am — for I also have become as you are. You have done me no wrong;
48_4_13: but you know that it was because of a bodily illness that I preached the gospel to you the first time.
48_4_14: And though my bodily condition was a trial to you, you did not despise or loathe me. But you received me as an angel of God — as Christ Jesus Himself.
48_4_15: Where then is that sense of blessing you had? For I bear you witness that, if possible, you would have plucked out your eyes and given them to me.
48_4_16: So have I become your enemy by telling you the truth?
48_4_17: They eagerly seek you — not commendably, but they want to shut you out, so that you will seek them.
48_4_18: But it is good always to be eagerly sought in a commendable manner — and not only when I am present with you.
48_4_19: My children, with whom I am again in labor pains until Christ is formed in you —
48_4_20: I would gladly be present with you now, and to change my tone — for I am perplexed about you.
48_4_21: Tell me, you who want to be under the Law — do you not listen to the Law?
48_4_22: For it is written that Abraham had two sons — one by the slave woman, and one by the free woman.
48_4_23: But the son by the slave woman was born according to the flesh — and the son by the free woman, through the promise.
48_4_24: These things are spoken allegorically — for these women are two covenants. One is from Mount Sinai, bearing children who are to be slaves — she is Hagar.
48_4_25: Now this Hagar represents Mount Sinai in Arabia — and corresponds to the present Jerusalem, for she is in slavery with her children.
48_4_26: But the Jerusalem above is free — she is our mother.
48_4_27: For it is written, "Rejoice, barren woman who does not bear; break forth and shout, you who are not in labor — for more numerous are the children of the desolate, than of the one who has a husband."
48_4_28: And we, brothers — like Isaac — are children of promise.
48_4_29: But just as at that time, the one who was born according to the flesh persecuted the one who was born according to the Spirit — so it is now also.
48_4_30: But what does the Scripture say? "Cast out the slave woman and her son — for the son of the slave woman shall not be an heir with the son of the free woman."
48_4_31: So then, brothers, we are not children of a slave woman, but of the free woman.
48_5_1: It was for freedom that Christ set us free. Therefore stand firm, and do not be subject again to a yoke of slavery.
48_5_2: Behold — I, Paul, say to you that if you receive circumcision, Christ will be of no benefit to you.
48_5_3: And I testify again to every man who receives circumcision, that he is under obligation to keep the whole Law.
48_5_4: You who are seeking to be justified by Law have been severed from Christ — you have fallen from grace.
48_5_5: For we, through the Spirit, by faith, are eagerly waiting for the hope of righteousness.
48_5_6: For in Christ Jesus, neither circumcision nor uncircumcision means anything — but only faith working through love.
48_5_7: You were running well; who hindered you from obeying the truth?
48_5_8: This persuasion did not come from the One who calls you.
48_5_9: A little leaven leavens the whole lump of dough.
48_5_10: I have confidence in you in the Lord, that you will adopt no other view. But the one who is disturbing you will bear his judgment, whoever he is.
48_5_11: But I, brothers — if I still preach circumcision, why am I still persecuted? Then the stumbling block of the cross has been abolished.
48_5_12: I wish that those who are troubling you would even mutilate themselves!
48_5_13: For you were called to freedom, brothers — only do not turn your freedom into an opportunity for the flesh, but through love serve one another.
48_5_14: For the whole Law is fulfilled in one word: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself."
48_5_15: But if you bite and devour one another, take care that you are not consumed by one another.
48_5_16: But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not carry out the desire of the flesh.
48_5_17: For the flesh sets its desire against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh — for these are in opposition to one another, so that you may not do the things you please.
48_5_18: But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the Law.
48_5_19: Now the deeds of the flesh are evident — sexual immorality, impurity, sensuality,
48_5_20: idolatry, sorcery, hostilities, strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, selfish ambition, dissensions, factions,
48_5_21: envying, drunkenness, carousing, and things like these — of which I forewarn you, just as I have forewarned you, that those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
48_5_22: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
48_5_23: gentleness, self-control. Against such things there is no law.
48_5_24: Now those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.
48_5_25: If we live by the Spirit, let us also walk by the Spirit.
48_5_26: Let us not become boastful, challenging one another, envying one another.
48_6_1: Brothers, even if anyone is caught in any trespass, you who are spiritual restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness — looking to yourself, so that you too will not be tempted.
48_6_2: Bear one another's burdens — and so fulfill the law of Christ.
48_6_3: For if anyone thinks he is something, when he is nothing — he deceives himself.
48_6_4: But each one must examine his own work — and then he will have reason for boasting in regard to himself alone, and not in regard to another.
48_6_5: For each one will bear his own load.
48_6_6: And the one who is taught the word is to share all good things with the one who teaches him.
48_6_7: Do not be deceived: God is not mocked. For whatever a man sows — this he will also reap.
48_6_8: For the one who sows to his own flesh will reap corruption from the flesh — but the one who sows to the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit.
48_6_9: Let us not lose heart in doing good. For in due time we will reap, if we do not grow weary.
48_6_10: So then, while we have opportunity, let us do good to all people — and especially to those who are of the household of the faith.
48_6_11: See with what large letters I am writing to you with my own hand!
48_6_12: Those who desire to make a good showing in the flesh — they try to compel you to be circumcised, simply so that they will not be persecuted for the cross of Christ.
48_6_13: For those who are circumcised do not even keep the Law themselves — but they desire to have you circumcised, so that they may boast in your flesh.
48_6_14: But may it never be that I should boast — except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ — through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
48_6_15: For neither is circumcision anything, nor uncircumcision — but a new creation.
48_6_16: And those who will walk by this rule — peace and mercy be upon them, and upon the Israel of God.
48_6_17: From now on, let no one cause trouble for me — for I bear on my body the brand-marks of Jesus.
48_6_18: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.
49_1_1: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God — to the saints who are at Ephesus, and who are faithful in Christ Jesus:
49_1_2: Grace to you, and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
49_1_3: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ — who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ.
49_1_4: Just as He chose us in Him, before the foundation of the world — that we would be holy and blameless before Him. In love
49_1_5: He predestined us to adoption as sons through Jesus Christ to Himself — according to the kind intention of His will,
49_1_6: to the praise of the glory of His grace — which He freely bestowed on us in the Beloved.
49_1_7: In Him we have redemption through His blood — the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of His grace,
49_1_8: which He lavished on us. In all wisdom and insight,
49_1_9: He made known to us the mystery of His will — according to His kind intention which He purposed in Him,
49_1_10: with a view to an administration suitable to the fullness of the times — to bring all things together in Christ, things in the heavens and things on the earth — in Him.
49_1_11: In Him also we have obtained an inheritance — having been predestined according to the purpose of Him who works all things after the counsel of His will,
49_1_12: so that we — who were the first to hope in Christ — would be to the praise of His glory.
49_1_13: In Him, you also, after listening to the message of truth — the gospel of your salvation — and after believing in Him, you were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise,
49_1_14: who is given as a pledge of our inheritance — until the redemption of God's own possession, to the praise of His glory.
49_1_15: For this reason, having heard of the faith in the Lord Jesus which is among you, and your love for all the saints,
49_1_16: I do not cease giving thanks for you — making mention of you in my prayers,
49_1_17: that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ — the Father of glory — may give to you a spirit of wisdom and of revelation in the knowledge of Him.
49_1_18: I pray that the eyes of your heart may be enlightened — so that you will know what is the hope of His calling, what are the riches of the glory of His inheritance in the saints,
49_1_19: and what is the surpassing greatness of His power toward us who believe — according to the working of the strength of His might,
49_1_20: which He brought about in Christ — when He raised Him from the dead, and seated Him at His right hand in the heavenly places,
49_1_21: far above all rule and authority and power and dominion — and every name that is named, not only in this age, but also in the one to come.
49_1_22: And He put all things in subjection under His feet — and gave Him as head over all things to the church,
49_1_23: which is His body — the fullness of Him who fills all in all.
49_2_1: And you were dead in your trespasses and sins —
49_2_2: in which you formerly walked, according to the course of this world — according to the prince of the power of the air, of the spirit that is now working in the sons of disobedience.
49_2_3: Among them we too all formerly conducted ourselves in the lusts of our flesh — indulging the desires of the flesh and of the mind. And we were by nature children of wrath — even as the rest.
49_2_4: But God, being rich in mercy — because of His great love with which He loved us,
49_2_5: even when we were dead in our transgressions, made us alive together with Christ. By grace you have been saved.
49_2_6: And He raised us up with Him, and seated us with Him in the heavenly places, in Christ Jesus —
49_2_7: so that in the ages to come He might show the surpassing riches of His grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus.
49_2_8: For by grace you have been saved through faith — and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God.
49_2_9: Not by works, so that no one may boast.
49_2_10: For we are His workmanship — created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand so that we would walk in them.
49_2_11: Therefore remember that formerly you, the Gentiles in the flesh, who are called "Uncircumcision" by the so-called "Circumcision," which is performed in the flesh by human hands —
49_2_12: remember that you were at that time separate from Christ, excluded from the commonwealth of Israel, strangers to the covenants of promise — having no hope, and without God in the world.
49_2_13: But now in Christ Jesus, you who were once far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ.
49_2_14: For He Himself is our peace — He who made the two groups one, and broke down the dividing wall of hostility,
49_2_15: by abolishing in His flesh the enmity — the Law of commandments contained in ordinances. He did this, so that in Himself He might make the two into one new man, thus making peace —
49_2_16: and might reconcile them both in one body to God through the cross — by it putting to death the enmity.
49_2_17: And He came and preached peace to you who were far off, and peace to those who were near.
49_2_18: For through Him, we both have our access in one Spirit to the Father.
49_2_19: So then, you are no longer strangers and aliens — but you are fellow citizens with the saints, and members of God's household.
49_2_20: You have been built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets — Christ Jesus Himself being the chief cornerstone.
49_2_21: In Him the whole building, being fitted together, is growing into a holy temple in the Lord —
49_2_22: in whom you also are being built together into a dwelling of God in the Spirit.
49_3_1: For this reason — I, Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus on behalf of you Gentiles —
49_3_2: if indeed you have heard of the stewardship of the grace of God which was given to me for you,
49_3_3: that by revelation there was made known to me the mystery — as I wrote before in brief.
49_3_4: By referring to this, when you read it, you can understand my insight into the mystery of Christ —
49_3_5: which in other generations was not made known to the sons of men, as it has now been revealed to His holy apostles and prophets in the Spirit.
49_3_6: This mystery: that the Gentiles are fellow heirs and fellow members of the body, and fellow partakers of the promise in Christ Jesus through the gospel.
49_3_7: Of this gospel I was made a minister — according to the gift of God's grace which was given to me, by the working of His power.
49_3_8: To me — the very least of all saints — this grace was given: to preach to the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ,
49_3_9: and to bring to light for everyone what is the administration of the mystery — which for ages has been hidden in God, who created all things.
49_3_10: So that the manifold wisdom of God might now be made known through the church — to the rulers and the authorities in the heavenly places —
49_3_11: in accordance with the eternal purpose which He carried out in Christ Jesus our Lord.
49_3_12: In Him we have boldness, and confident access through faith in Him.
49_3_13: Therefore I ask that you do not lose heart at my tribulations on your behalf — for they are your glory.
49_3_14: For this reason, I bow my knees before the Father —
49_3_15: from whom every family in heaven and on earth derives its name —
49_3_16: that He would grant you, according to the riches of His glory, to be strengthened with power through His Spirit in the inner man,
49_3_17: so that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith — being rooted and grounded in love.
49_3_18: May you be able to comprehend, with all the saints, what is the breadth and length and height and depth —
49_3_19: and to know the love of Christ which surpasses knowledge — that you may be filled up to all the fullness of God.
49_3_20: Now to Him who is able to do far more abundantly beyond all that we ask or think — according to the power that works within us —
49_3_21: to Him be the glory in the church and in Christ Jesus, to all generations forever and ever. Amen.
49_4_1: Therefore I, the prisoner in the Lord, urge you to walk in a manner worthy of the calling with which you have been called —
49_4_2: with all humility and gentleness, with patience — bearing with one another in love,
49_4_3: being diligent to preserve the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
49_4_4: There is one body, and one Spirit — just as you also were called in one hope of your calling;
49_4_5: one Lord, one faith, one baptism;
49_4_6: one God and Father of all — who is over all and through all and in all.
49_4_7: But to each one of us grace was given according to the measure of Christ's gift.
49_4_8: Therefore it says, "When He ascended on high, He led captive a host of captives, and He gave gifts to men."
49_4_9: (Now this expression, "He ascended" — what does it mean except that He also descended into the lower parts of the earth?
49_4_10: He who descended is Himself also the One who ascended far above all the heavens — so that He might fill all things.)
49_4_11: And He gave some as apostles, some as prophets, some as evangelists, and some as pastors and teachers,
49_4_12: for the equipping of the saints for the work of service — to the building up of the body of Christ;
49_4_13: until we all attain to the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God — to a mature man, to the measure of the stature which belongs to the fullness of Christ.
49_4_14: As a result, we are no longer to be children — tossed here and there by waves and carried about by every wind of doctrine, by the trickery of men, by craftiness in deceitful scheming.
49_4_15: But speaking the truth in love, we are to grow up in all aspects into Him — who is the head, even Christ.
49_4_16: From Him, the whole body — being fitted and held together by what every joint supplies, according to the proper working of each individual part — causes the growth of the body, for the building up of itself in love.
49_4_17: So this I say, and affirm together with the Lord: that you walk no longer just as the Gentiles also walk — in the futility of their mind,
49_4_18: being darkened in their understanding, excluded from the life of God, because of the ignorance that is in them — because of the hardness of their heart.
49_4_19: And they, having become callous, have given themselves over to sensuality — for the practice of every kind of impurity, with greediness.
49_4_20: But you did not learn Christ in this way —
49_4_21: if indeed you have heard Him and have been taught in Him, just as truth is in Jesus.
49_4_22: That, in reference to your former manner of life, you lay aside the old self — which is being corrupted in accordance with the lusts of deceit,
49_4_23: and that you be renewed in the spirit of your mind,
49_4_24: and put on the new self — which in the likeness of God has been created in righteousness and holiness of the truth.
49_4_25: Therefore, laying aside falsehood, speak truth each one of you with his neighbor — for we are members of one another.
49_4_26: Be angry, and yet do not sin. Do not let the sun go down on your anger,
49_4_27: and do not give the devil an opportunity.
49_4_28: He who steals must steal no longer — but rather, he must labor, performing with his own hands what is good, so that he will have something to share with one who has need.
49_4_29: Let no unwholesome word come out of your mouth — but only such a word as is good for edification according to the need of the moment, so that it will give grace to those who hear.
49_4_30: And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God — by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.
49_4_31: Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamor, and slander be put away from you — along with all malice.
49_4_32: And be kind to one another, tender-hearted — forgiving one another, just as God in Christ also has forgiven you.
49_5_1: Therefore be imitators of God — as beloved children;
49_5_2: and walk in love — just as Christ also loved you and gave Himself up for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God as a fragrant aroma.
49_5_3: But sexual immorality, or any impurity, or greed must not even be named among you — as is proper among saints.
49_5_4: And there must be no filthiness, and no silly talk, or coarse jesting — which are not fitting; but rather, giving of thanks.
49_5_5: For this you know with certainty: that no immoral or impure person, or covetous man (who is an idolater), has an inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God.
49_5_6: Let no one deceive you with empty words — for because of these things, the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience.
49_5_7: Therefore do not be partakers with them.
49_5_8: For you were formerly darkness — but now you are light in the Lord. Walk as children of light
49_5_9: (for the fruit of the light consists in all goodness, and righteousness, and truth),
49_5_10: trying to discover what is pleasing to the Lord.
49_5_11: And do not participate in the unfruitful deeds of darkness — but instead, even expose them.
49_5_12: For it is disgraceful even to speak of the things which are done by them in secret.
49_5_13: But all things become visible when they are exposed by the light — for everything that becomes visible is light.
49_5_14: For this reason it says, "Awake, sleeper, and arise from the dead — and Christ will shine on you."
49_5_15: Therefore, be careful how you walk — not as unwise men, but as wise,
49_5_16: making the most of your time, because the days are evil.
49_5_17: So then, do not be foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord is.
49_5_18: And do not get drunk with wine, in which is dissipation — but be filled with the Spirit,
49_5_19: speaking to one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs — singing and making melody with your heart to the Lord;
49_5_20: always giving thanks for all things — in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ — to God, even the Father.
49_5_21: And be subject to one another in the fear of Christ.
49_5_22: Wives, be subject to your own husbands, as to the Lord.
49_5_23: For the husband is the head of the wife — as Christ also is the head of the church, He Himself being the Savior of the body.
49_5_24: But as the church is subject to Christ, so also the wives ought to be to their husbands in everything.
49_5_25: Husbands, love your wives — just as Christ also loved the church and gave Himself up for her,
49_5_26: so that He might sanctify her — having cleansed her by the washing of water with the word,
49_5_27: that He might present to Himself the church in all her glory — having no spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that she would be holy and blameless.
49_5_28: So husbands ought also to love their own wives as their own bodies. He who loves his own wife loves himself.
49_5_29: For no one ever hated his own flesh — but nourishes and cherishes it, just as Christ also does the church,
49_5_30: because we are members of His body.
49_5_31: For this reason, a man shall leave his father and mother, and shall be joined to his wife — and the two shall become one flesh.
49_5_32: This mystery is great — but I am speaking with reference to Christ and the church.
49_5_33: Nevertheless, each individual among you also is to love his own wife as he loves himself — and the wife must see to it that she respects her husband.
49_6_1: Children, obey your parents in the Lord — for this is right.
49_6_2: "Honor your father and mother" — which is the first commandment with a promise —
49_6_3: "so that it may be well with you, and that you may live long on the earth."
49_6_4: And fathers, do not provoke your children to anger — but bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.
49_6_5: Bondservants, be obedient to those who are your masters according to the flesh — with fear and trembling, in the sincerity of your heart, as to Christ.
49_6_6: Not by way of eye-service, as men-pleasers — but as bondservants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart.
49_6_7: With good will render service — as to the Lord, and not to men,
49_6_8: knowing that whatever good thing each one does, this he will receive back from the Lord — whether slave or free.
49_6_9: And masters, do the same things to them — and give up threatening, knowing that both their Master and yours is in heaven, and there is no partiality with Him.
49_6_10: Finally, be strong in the Lord and in the strength of His might.
49_6_11: Put on the full armor of God — so that you will be able to stand firm against the schemes of the devil.
49_6_12: For our struggle is not against flesh and blood — but against the rulers, against the powers, against the world forces of this darkness, against the spiritual forces of wickedness in the heavenly places.
49_6_13: Therefore, take up the full armor of God — so that you will be able to resist in the evil day, and having done everything, to stand firm.
49_6_14: Stand firm therefore — having girded your loins with truth, and having put on the breastplate of righteousness,
49_6_15: and having shod your feet with the readiness of the gospel of peace.
49_6_16: In addition to all, taking up the shield of faith — with which you will be able to extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one.
49_6_17: And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit — which is the word of God.
49_6_18: With all prayer and petition, pray at all times in the Spirit — and with this in view, be on the alert with all perseverance and petition for all the saints,
49_6_19: and pray on my behalf — that words may be given to me in the opening of my mouth, to make known with boldness the mystery of the gospel,
49_6_20: for which I am an ambassador in chains — that in proclaiming it, I may speak boldly, as I ought to speak.
49_6_21: But that you also may know about my circumstances, how I am doing — Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord, will make everything known to you.
49_6_22: I have sent him to you for this very purpose — so that you may know about us, and that he may comfort your hearts.
49_6_23: Peace be to the brothers, and love with faith — from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
49_6_24: Grace be with all those who love our Lord Jesus Christ with incorruptible love. Amen.
47_1_1: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Timothy our brother — to the church of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints who are throughout Achaia:
47_1_2: Grace to you, and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
47_1_3: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ — the Father of mercies and God of all comfort,
47_1_4: who comforts us in all our affliction — so that we will be able to comfort those who are in any affliction, with the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.
47_1_5: For just as the sufferings of Christ are ours in abundance, so also our comfort is abundant through Christ.
47_1_6: But if we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation; or if we are comforted, it is for your comfort — which is effective in the patient enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer.
47_1_7: And our hope for you is firmly grounded — knowing that as you are sharers of our sufferings, so also you are sharers of our comfort.
47_1_8: For we do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of our affliction which came to us in Asia — that we were burdened excessively, beyond our strength, so that we despaired even of life.
47_1_9: Indeed, we had the sentence of death within ourselves — so that we would not trust in ourselves, but in God who raises the dead.
47_1_10: He delivered us from so great a peril of death, and will deliver us. He on whom we have set our hope — and He will yet deliver us.
47_1_11: You also are joining in helping us through your prayers — so that thanks may be given by many persons on our behalf, for the favor bestowed on us through the prayers of many.
47_1_12: For our proud confidence is this: the testimony of our conscience, that in holiness and godly sincerity — not in fleshly wisdom, but in the grace of God — we have conducted ourselves in the world, and especially toward you.
47_1_13: For we write nothing else to you than what you read and understand. And I hope you will understand fully —
47_1_14: just as you also partially did understand us — that we are your reason to be proud, as you also are ours, in the day of our Lord Jesus.
47_1_15: In this confidence, I intended at first to come to you — so that you might twice receive a blessing.
47_1_16: And to pass through your way to Macedonia, and again from Macedonia to come to you — and by you, to be helped on my way to Judea.
47_1_17: Therefore, I was not vacillating when I intended to do this, was I? Or what I purpose, do I purpose according to the flesh — so that with me there will be both "yes, yes" and "no, no"?
47_1_18: But as God is faithful, our word to you is not yes and no.
47_1_19: For the Son of God, Christ Jesus — who was preached among you by us, by me and Silvanus and Timothy — was not yes and no, but is yes in Him.
47_1_20: For as many as are the promises of God, in Him they are yes — and in Him they are amen, to the glory of God through us.
47_1_21: Now He who establishes us with you in Christ, and anointed us, is God,
47_1_22: who also sealed us, and gave us the Spirit in our hearts as a pledge.
47_1_23: But I call God as witness against my soul, that to spare you I did not come again to Corinth.
47_1_24: Not that we lord it over your faith — but we are workers with you for your joy. For in your faith you stand firm.
47_2_1: But I determined this for my own sake — that I would not come to you in sorrow again.
47_2_2: For if I cause you sorrow, who then makes me glad — except the one whom I made sorrowful?
47_2_3: And I wrote this very thing to you, so that when I came, I would not have sorrow from those who ought to make me rejoice — having confidence in you all that my joy would be the joy of you all.
47_2_4: For out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote to you, with many tears — not so that you would be made sorrowful, but so that you might know the love which I have especially for you.
47_2_5: But if any has caused sorrow, he has caused sorrow not to me, but in some degree — in order not to say too much — to all of you.
47_2_6: Sufficient for such a one is this punishment which was inflicted by the majority.
47_2_7: So on the contrary, you should rather forgive and comfort him — otherwise, such a one might be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow.
47_2_8: Therefore I urge you to reaffirm your love for him.
47_2_9: For to this end also I wrote — so that I might put you to the test, whether you are obedient in all things.
47_2_10: But one whom you forgive anything, I forgive also. For indeed, what I have forgiven — if I have forgiven anything — I did it for your sakes in the presence of Christ,
47_2_11: so that no advantage would be taken of us by Satan — for we are not ignorant of his schemes.
47_2_12: Now when I came to Troas for the gospel of Christ, and when a door was opened for me in the Lord,
47_2_13: I had no rest for my spirit — not finding Titus my brother. But taking my leave of them, I went on to Macedonia.
47_2_14: But thanks be to God — who always leads us in triumph in Christ, and through us spreads the fragrance of the knowledge of Him in every place.
47_2_15: For we are a fragrance of Christ to God among those who are being saved, and among those who are perishing —
47_2_16: to the one, an aroma from death to death; to the other, an aroma from life to life. And who is adequate for these things?
47_2_17: For we are not, like so many, peddling the word of God. But as from sincerity — but as from God — we speak in Christ in the sight of God.
47_3_1: Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or do we need, as some, letters of commendation to you, or from you?
47_3_2: You are our letter, written in our hearts — known and read by all men;
47_3_3: being manifested as a letter of Christ, cared for by us — written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not on tablets of stone, but on tablets of human hearts.
47_3_4: Such confidence we have through Christ toward God.
47_3_5: Not that we are adequate in ourselves to consider anything as coming from ourselves — but our adequacy is from God,
47_3_6: who also made us adequate as servants of a new covenant — not of the letter, but of the Spirit. For the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.
47_3_7: But if the ministry of death — in letters engraved on stones — came with glory, so that the sons of Israel could not look intently at the face of Moses because of the glory of his face, fading as it was —
47_3_8: how will the ministry of the Spirit fail to be even more in glory?
47_3_9: For if the ministry of condemnation has glory, much more does the ministry of righteousness abound in glory.
47_3_10: For indeed, what had glory has no glory in this case — because of the glory that surpasses it.
47_3_11: For if that which fades away was with glory, much more that which remains is in glory.
47_3_12: Therefore, having such a hope, we use great boldness in our speech.
47_3_13: And we are not like Moses — who used to put a veil over his face, so that the sons of Israel would not look intently at the end of what was fading away.
47_3_14: But their minds were hardened. For until this very day, at the reading of the old covenant the same veil remains unlifted — because it is removed in Christ.
47_3_15: But to this day, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies over their heart.
47_3_16: But whenever a person turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
47_3_17: Now the Lord is the Spirit — and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.
47_3_18: But we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord — are being transformed into the same image, from glory to glory — just as from the Lord, the Spirit.
47_4_1: Therefore, since we have this ministry — as we received mercy — we do not lose heart.
47_4_2: But we have renounced the things hidden because of shame — not walking in craftiness, or adulterating the word of God. But by the manifestation of truth, we commend ourselves to every man's conscience in the sight of God.
47_4_3: And even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled to those who are perishing —
47_4_4: in whose case the god of this age has blinded the minds of the unbelieving — so that they might not see the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.
47_4_5: For we do not preach ourselves, but Christ Jesus as Lord — and ourselves as your bondservants for Jesus' sake.
47_4_6: For God, who said, "Light shall shine out of darkness," is the One who has shone in our hearts — to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Christ.
47_4_7: But we have this treasure in earthen vessels — so that the surpassing greatness of the power will be of God, and not from ourselves.
47_4_8: We are afflicted in every way, but not crushed; perplexed, but not despairing;
47_4_9: persecuted, but not forsaken; struck down, but not destroyed —
47_4_10: always carrying about in the body the dying of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus also may be manifested in our body.
47_4_11: For we who live are constantly being delivered over to death for Jesus' sake — so that the life of Jesus also may be manifested in our mortal flesh.
47_4_12: So death works in us, but life in you.
47_4_13: But having the same spirit of faith, according to what is written, "I believed; therefore I spoke," we also believe — therefore we also speak.
47_4_14: Knowing that He who raised the Lord Jesus will raise us also with Jesus, and will present us with you.
47_4_15: For all things are for your sakes — so that the grace, which is spreading to more and more people, may cause the giving of thanks to abound to the glory of God.
47_4_16: Therefore we do not lose heart. But though our outer man is decaying, yet our inner man is being renewed day by day.
47_4_17: For our momentary, light affliction is producing for us an eternal weight of glory far beyond all comparison —
47_4_18: while we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal.
47_5_1: For we know that if our earthly tent — which is our house — is torn down, we have a building from God, a house not made with hands — eternal in the heavens.
47_5_2: For indeed, in this house we groan — longing to be clothed with our dwelling from heaven.
47_5_3: Inasmuch as we, having put it on, will not be found naked.
47_5_4: For indeed, while we are in this tent, we groan, being burdened — because we do not want to be unclothed, but to be clothed, so that what is mortal will be swallowed up by life.
47_5_5: Now He who prepared us for this very purpose is God — who gave to us the Spirit as a pledge.
47_5_6: Therefore, being always of good courage — and knowing that while we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord —
47_5_7: for we walk by faith, not by sight.
47_5_8: We are of good courage, I say, and prefer rather to be absent from the body and to be at home with the Lord.
47_5_9: Therefore we also have as our ambition, whether at home or absent, to be pleasing to Him.
47_5_10: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ — so that each one may be recompensed for his deeds in the body, according to what he has done, whether good or bad.
47_5_11: Therefore, knowing the fear of the Lord, we persuade men. But we are made manifest to God — and I hope that we are made manifest also in your consciences.
47_5_12: We are not again commending ourselves to you — but are giving you an occasion to be proud of us, so that you will have an answer for those who take pride in appearance and not in heart.
47_5_13: For if we are beside ourselves, it is for God; if we are of sound mind, it is for you.
47_5_14: For the love of Christ controls us — having concluded this: that one died for all, therefore all died.
47_5_15: And He died for all, so that they who live might no longer live for themselves — but for Him who died and rose again on their behalf.
47_5_16: Therefore from now on, we recognize no one according to the flesh. Even though we have known Christ according to the flesh, yet now we know Him in this way no longer.
47_5_17: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away — behold, new things have come!
47_5_18: Now all these things are from God — who reconciled us to Himself through Christ, and gave us the ministry of reconciliation.
47_5_19: Namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to Himself — not counting their trespasses against them — and He has committed to us the word of reconciliation.
47_5_20: Therefore, we are ambassadors for Christ — as though God were making an appeal through us. We beg you on behalf of Christ: be reconciled to God.
47_5_21: He made Him who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf — so that we might become the righteousness of God in Him.
47_6_1: And working together with Him, we also urge you not to receive the grace of God in vain —
47_6_2: for He says, "At the acceptable time I listened to you, and on the day of salvation I helped you." Behold — now is the acceptable time! Behold — now is the day of salvation!
47_6_3: Giving no cause for offense in anything — so that the ministry will not be discredited —
47_6_4: but in everything, commending ourselves as servants of God: in much endurance, in afflictions, in hardships, in distresses,
47_6_5: in beatings, in imprisonments, in tumults, in labors, in sleeplessness, in hunger,
47_6_6: in purity, in knowledge, in patience, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in genuine love;
47_6_7: in the word of truth, in the power of God; by the weapons of righteousness for the right hand and the left,
47_6_8: by glory and dishonor, by evil report and good report; regarded as deceivers — and yet true;
47_6_9: as unknown — yet well known; as dying — yet behold, we live; as punished — yet not put to death;
47_6_10: as sorrowful — yet always rejoicing; as poor — yet making many rich; as having nothing — yet possessing all things.
47_6_11: Our mouth has spoken freely to you, O Corinthians. Our heart is opened wide.
47_6_12: You are not restrained by us, but you are restrained in your own affections.
47_6_13: Now in a like exchange — I speak as to children — open wide to us also.
47_6_14: Do not be bound together with unbelievers — for what partnership have righteousness and lawlessness, or what fellowship has light with darkness?
47_6_15: Or what harmony has Christ with Belial, or what has a believer in common with an unbeliever?
47_6_16: Or what agreement has the temple of God with idols? For we are the temple of the living God — just as God said: "I will dwell among them, and walk among them; and I will be their God, and they shall be My people."
47_6_17: "Therefore, come out from their midst, and be separate," says the Lord, "and do not touch what is unclean — and I will welcome you.
47_6_18: And I will be a Father to you, and you shall be sons and daughters to Me," says the Lord Almighty.
47_7_1: Therefore, having these promises, beloved — let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement of flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.
47_7_2: Make room for us in your hearts. We wronged no one. We corrupted no one. We took advantage of no one.
47_7_3: I do not speak to condemn you — for I have said before that you are in our hearts, to die together and to live together.
47_7_4: Great is my confidence in you. Great is my boasting on your behalf. I am filled with comfort. I am overflowing with joy in all our affliction.
47_7_5: For even when we came into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest — but we were afflicted on every side: conflicts without, fears within.
47_7_6: But God, who comforts the depressed, comforted us by the coming of Titus.
47_7_7: And not only by his coming, but also by the comfort with which he was comforted in you — as he reported to us your longing, your mourning, your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced even more.
47_7_8: For though I caused you sorrow by my letter, I do not regret it. Though I did regret it — for I see that that letter caused you sorrow, though only for a while —
47_7_9: I now rejoice — not that you were made sorrowful, but that you were made sorrowful to the point of repentance. For you were made sorrowful according to the will of God — so that you might not suffer loss in anything through us.
47_7_10: For the sorrow that is according to the will of God produces a repentance leading to salvation, without regret. But the sorrow of the world produces death.
47_7_11: For behold, what earnestness this very thing — this godly sorrow — has produced in you. What vindication of yourselves! What indignation! What fear! What longing! What zeal! What avenging of wrong! In everything, you demonstrated yourselves to be innocent in the matter.
47_7_12: So although I wrote to you, it was not for the sake of the offender, nor for the sake of the one offended — but that your earnestness on our behalf might be made known to you in the sight of God.
47_7_13: For this reason we have been comforted. And besides our comfort, we rejoiced even much more for the joy of Titus, because his spirit has been refreshed by you all.
47_7_14: For if in anything I have boasted to him about you, I was not put to shame — but as we spoke all things to you in truth, so also our boasting before Titus proved to be the truth.
47_7_15: And his affection abounds all the more toward you, as he remembers the obedience of you all — how you received him with fear and trembling.
47_7_16: I rejoice that in everything I have confidence in you.
47_8_1: Now, brothers, we wish to make known to you the grace of God which has been given in the churches of Macedonia —
47_8_2: that in a great ordeal of affliction, their abundance of joy and their deep poverty overflowed in the wealth of their liberality.
47_8_3: For I testify that according to their ability, and beyond their ability, they gave of their own accord —
47_8_4: begging us with much urging for the favor of participation in the support of the saints.
47_8_5: And not as we had expected — but they first gave themselves to the Lord, and to us by the will of God.
47_8_6: So we urged Titus, that as he had previously begun, so he would also complete in you this gracious work as well.
47_8_7: But just as you abound in everything — in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in all earnestness, and in the love we inspired in you — see that you abound in this gracious work also.
47_8_8: I am not speaking this as a command — but as proving, through the earnestness of others, the sincerity of your love also.
47_8_9: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ — that though He was rich, yet for your sake He became poor, so that you, through His poverty, might become rich.
47_8_10: I give my opinion in this matter — for this is to your advantage, who were the first to begin a year ago, not only to do this, but also to desire to do it.
47_8_11: But now finish doing it also — so that just as there was the readiness to desire it, so there may also be the completion of it according to your ability.
47_8_12: For if the readiness is present, it is acceptable according to what a person has — not according to what he does not have.
47_8_13: For this is not for the ease of others and for your affliction — but by way of equality.
47_8_14: At this present time, your abundance being a supply for their need, so that their abundance may also become a supply for your need — that there may be equality.
47_8_15: As it is written, "He who gathered much did not have too much, and he who gathered little did not have too little."
47_8_16: But thanks be to God — who puts the same earnestness on your behalf in the heart of Titus.
47_8_17: For he not only accepted our appeal — but being himself very earnest, he has gone to you of his own accord.
47_8_18: And we have sent along with him the brother whose fame in the things of the gospel has spread through all the churches.
47_8_19: Not only this — but he was also appointed by the churches to travel with us in this gracious work, which is being administered by us — to the glory of the Lord Himself, and to show our readiness.
47_8_20: Taking precaution so that no one will discredit us in our administration of this generous gift.
47_8_21: For we have regard for what is honorable — not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.
47_8_22: And we have sent with them our brother — whom we have often tested and found diligent in many things, but now even more diligent because of his great confidence in you.
47_8_23: As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker among you — as for our brothers, they are messengers of the churches, a glory to Christ.
47_8_24: Therefore, openly before the churches, show them the proof of your love and of our reason for boasting about you.
47_9_1: For it is superfluous for me to write to you about this ministry to the saints —
47_9_2: for I know your readiness — of which I boast about you to the Macedonians, namely, that Achaia has been prepared since last year. And your zeal has stirred up most of them.
47_9_3: But I have sent the brothers — so that our boasting about you may not be made empty in this case, that, as I was saying, you may be prepared.
47_9_4: Otherwise, if any Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we — not to speak of you — would be put to shame by this confidence.
47_9_5: So I thought it necessary to urge the brothers that they would go on ahead to you, and arrange beforehand your previously promised bountiful gift — so that the same would be ready as a bountiful gift, and not affected by covetousness.
47_9_6: Now this I say: he who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly — and he who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.
47_9_7: Each one must do just as he has purposed in his heart — not grudgingly or under compulsion. For God loves a cheerful giver.
47_9_8: And God is able to make all grace abound to you — so that always having all sufficiency in everything, you may have an abundance for every good deed.
47_9_9: As it is written, "He scattered abroad, He gave to the poor; His righteousness endures forever."
47_9_10: Now He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food, will supply and multiply your seed for sowing — and increase the harvest of your righteousness.
47_9_11: You will be enriched in everything for all liberality — which through us is producing thanksgiving to God.
47_9_12: For the ministry of this service is not only fully supplying the needs of the saints — but is also overflowing through many thanksgivings to God.
47_9_13: Because of the proof given by this ministry, they will glorify God for your obedience to your confession of the gospel of Christ — and for the liberality of your contribution to them and to all,
47_9_14: while they also, by prayer on your behalf, yearn for you because of the surpassing grace of God in you.
47_9_15: Thanks be to God for His indescribable gift!
47_10_1: Now I, Paul, myself urge you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ — I who am meek when face to face with you, but bold toward you when absent!
47_10_2: I ask that when I am present I need not be bold with the confidence with which I propose to be courageous against some — who regard us as if we walked according to the flesh.
47_10_3: For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war according to the flesh.
47_10_4: For the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh — but divinely powerful for the destruction of strongholds.
47_10_5: We are destroying speculations and every lofty thing raised up against the knowledge of God — and we are taking every thought captive to the obedience of Christ.
47_10_6: And we are ready to punish all disobedience, whenever your obedience is complete.
