47_10_7: You are looking at things as they are outwardly. If anyone is confident in himself that he is Christ's, let him consider this again within himself: that just as he is Christ's, so also are we.
47_10_8: For even if I boast somewhat further about our authority — which the Lord gave for building you up and not for tearing you down — I will not be put to shame.
47_10_9: For I do not wish to seem as if I would terrify you by my letters.
47_10_10: For they say, "His letters are weighty and strong, but his personal presence is unimpressive, and his speech contemptible."
47_10_11: Let such a person consider this: that what we are in word by letters when absent, such persons we are also in deed when present.
47_10_12: For we are not bold to class or compare ourselves with some of those who commend themselves. But when they measure themselves by themselves, and compare themselves with themselves, they are without understanding.
47_10_13: But we will not boast beyond our measure — but within the measure of the sphere which God apportioned to us as a measure, to reach even as far as you.
47_10_14: For we are not overextending ourselves — as if we did not reach to you. For we were the first to come even as far as you, in the gospel of Christ.
47_10_15: Not boasting beyond our measure — that is, in other men's labors. But with the hope that as your faith grows, we will be, within our sphere, enlarged even more by you,
47_10_16: so as to preach the gospel even to the regions beyond you — and not to boast in what has been accomplished in the sphere of another.
47_10_17: But "he who boasts is to boast in the Lord."
47_10_18: For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved — but the one whom the Lord commends.
47_11_1: I wish that you would bear with me in a little foolishness. But indeed, you are bearing with me.
47_11_2: For I am jealous for you with a godly jealousy — for I betrothed you to one husband, that I might present you as a pure virgin to Christ.
47_11_3: But I am afraid that, as the serpent deceived Eve by his craftiness, your minds will be led astray from the simplicity and purity of devotion to Christ.
47_11_4: For if one comes and preaches another Jesus whom we have not preached, or you receive a different spirit which you have not received, or a different gospel which you have not accepted — you bear this beautifully.
47_11_5: For I consider myself not in the least inferior to the most eminent apostles.
47_11_6: But even if I am unskilled in speech, yet I am not in knowledge. In every way we have made this evident to you in all things.
47_11_7: Or did I commit a sin in humbling myself, so that you might be exalted, because I preached the gospel of God to you without charge?
47_11_8: I robbed other churches by taking wages from them to serve you.
47_11_9: And when I was present with you and was in need, I was not a burden to anyone — for when the brothers came from Macedonia, they fully supplied my need. And in everything I kept myself from being a burden to you, and will continue to do so.
47_11_10: As the truth of Christ is in me — this boasting of mine will not be stopped in the regions of Achaia.
47_11_11: Why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do!
47_11_12: But what I am doing, I will continue to do — so that I may cut off opportunity from those who desire an opportunity to be regarded just as we are in the matter about which they are boasting.
47_11_13: For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, disguising themselves as apostles of Christ.
47_11_14: And no wonder — for even Satan disguises himself as an angel of light.
47_11_15: Therefore it is not surprising if his servants also disguise themselves as servants of righteousness — whose end will be according to their deeds.
47_11_16: Again I say, let no one think me foolish. But if you do, receive me even as foolish — so that I also may boast a little.
47_11_17: What I am saying, I am not saying as the Lord would, but as in foolishness — in this confidence of boasting.
47_11_18: Since many boast according to the flesh, I will boast also.
47_11_19: For you, being so wise, tolerate the foolish gladly.
47_11_20: For you tolerate it if anyone enslaves you, anyone devours you, anyone takes advantage of you, anyone exalts himself, anyone strikes you in the face.
47_11_21: To my shame I must say that we have been weak by comparison. But in whatever respect anyone else is bold — I speak in foolishness — I am just as bold myself.
47_11_22: Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I.
47_11_23: Are they servants of Christ? — I speak as if insane — I more so. In far more labors, in far more imprisonments, beaten times without number, often in danger of death.
47_11_24: Five times I received from the Jews thirty-nine lashes.
47_11_25: Three times I was beaten with rods. Once I was stoned. Three times I was shipwrecked. A night and a day I have spent in the deep.
47_11_26: I have been on frequent journeys — in dangers from rivers, dangers from robbers, dangers from my countrymen, dangers from the Gentiles, dangers in the city, dangers in the wilderness, dangers on the sea, dangers among false brothers.
47_11_27: I have been in labor and hardship, through many sleepless nights, in hunger and thirst, often without food, in cold and exposure.
47_11_28: Apart from such external things — there is the daily pressure on me of concern for all the churches.
47_11_29: Who is weak without my being weak? Who is led into sin without my intense concern?
47_11_30: If I have to boast, I will boast of what pertains to my weakness.
47_11_31: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus — He who is blessed forever — knows that I am not lying.
47_11_32: In Damascus, the ethnarch under Aretas the king was guarding the city of the Damascenes in order to seize me.
47_11_33: And I was let down through a window in a basket through the wall — and so escaped his hands.
47_12_1: Boasting is necessary, though it is not profitable. But I will go on to visions and revelations of the Lord.
47_12_2: I know a man in Christ — who fourteen years ago was caught up to the third heaven (whether in the body, I do not know; or out of the body, I do not know — God knows).
47_12_3: And I know how such a man — whether in the body, or apart from the body, I do not know; God knows —
47_12_4: was caught up into Paradise, and heard inexpressible words, which a man is not permitted to speak.
47_12_5: On behalf of such a man I will boast — but on my own behalf I will not boast, except in regard to my weaknesses.
47_12_6: For if I do wish to boast, I will not be foolish — for I will be speaking the truth. But I refrain from this, so that no one will credit me with more than he sees in me, or hears from me.
47_12_7: Because of the surpassing greatness of the revelations — for this reason, to keep me from exalting myself, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, a messenger of Satan to torment me — to keep me from exalting myself!
47_12_8: Concerning this I implored the Lord three times, that it might leave me.
47_12_9: And He has said to me, "My grace is sufficient for you — for power is perfected in weakness." Most gladly therefore, I will rather boast about my weaknesses — so that the power of Christ may dwell in me.
47_12_10: Therefore, I am well content with weaknesses, with insults, with distresses, with persecutions, with difficulties — for Christ's sake. For when I am weak, then I am strong.
47_12_11: I have become foolish — you yourselves compelled me. Actually I should have been commended by you, for in no respect was I inferior to the most eminent apostles, even though I am a nobody.
47_12_12: The signs of a true apostle were performed among you with all perseverance — by signs and wonders and miracles.
47_12_13: For in what respect were you treated as inferior to the rest of the churches, except that I myself did not become a burden to you? Forgive me this wrong!
47_12_14: Behold — for the third time, I am ready to come to you, and I will not be a burden to you. For I do not seek what is yours, but you. For children are not responsible to save up for their parents — but parents for their children.
47_12_15: And I will most gladly spend, and be expended, for your souls. If I love you more, am I to be loved less?
47_12_16: But be that as it may — I did not burden you myself. Nevertheless, crafty fellow that I am, I took you in by deceit.
47_12_17: Certainly I have not taken advantage of you through any of those whom I have sent to you, have I?
47_12_18: I urged Titus to go, and I sent the brother with him. Titus did not take any advantage of you, did he? Did we not conduct ourselves in the same spirit, and walk in the same steps?
47_12_19: All this time, you have been thinking that we are defending ourselves to you. Actually it is in the sight of God that we have been speaking in Christ — and all for your upbuilding, beloved.
47_12_20: For I am afraid that perhaps when I come, I may find you to be not what I wish, and may be found by you to be not what you wish — that perhaps there will be strife, jealousy, angry tempers, disputes, slanders, gossip, arrogance, disturbances.
47_12_21: I am afraid that when I come again, my God may humiliate me before you — and I may mourn over many of those who have sinned in the past, and not repented of the impurity, immorality, and sensuality which they have practiced.
47_13_1: This is the third time I am coming to you. "Every fact is to be confirmed by the testimony of two or three witnesses."
47_13_2: I have previously said, when present the second time, and though now absent I say in advance to those who have sinned in the past, and to all the rest as well — that if I come again, I will not spare anyone.
47_13_3: Since you are seeking for proof of the Christ who speaks in me — and who is not weak toward you, but mighty in you.
47_13_4: For indeed, He was crucified because of weakness — yet He lives because of the power of God. For we also are weak in Him, yet we will live with Him because of the power of God directed toward you.
47_13_5: Test yourselves, to see if you are in the faith. Examine yourselves! Or do you not recognize about yourselves that Jesus Christ is in you — unless indeed you fail the test?
47_13_6: But I trust that you will realize that we ourselves do not fail the test.
47_13_7: Now we pray to God that you do no wrong — not so that we ourselves may appear approved, but that you may do what is right, even though we may appear unapproved.
47_13_8: For we can do nothing against the truth, but only for the truth.
47_13_9: For we rejoice when we ourselves are weak, but you are strong. This we also pray for: that you be made complete.
47_13_10: For this reason I am writing these things while absent — so that when present I will not need to use severity, in accordance with the authority which the Lord gave me, for building up and not for tearing down.
47_13_11: Finally, brothers, rejoice. Be made complete. Be comforted. Be like-minded. Live in peace — and the God of love and peace will be with you.
47_13_12: Greet one another with a holy kiss.
47_13_14: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all.
58_1_1: God, after He spoke long ago to the fathers in the prophets — in many parts and in many ways —
58_1_2: in these last days has spoken to us in His Son. He appointed Him heir of all things, through whom He also made the world.
58_1_3: And He is the radiance of His glory, and the exact representation of His nature — and He upholds all things by the word of His power. When He had made purification of sins, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.
58_1_4: Having become as much better than the angels, as He has inherited a more excellent name than they.
58_1_5: For to which of the angels did He ever say, "You are My Son, today I have begotten You"? And again, "I will be a Father to Him, and He shall be a Son to Me"?
58_1_6: And when He again brings the firstborn into the world, He says, "And let all the angels of God worship Him."
58_1_7: And of the angels He says, "He makes His angels winds, and His ministers a flame of fire."
58_1_8: But of the Son He says, "Your throne, O God, is forever and ever — and the scepter of righteousness is the scepter of His kingdom.
58_1_9: You have loved righteousness and hated lawlessness — therefore God, Your God, has anointed You with the oil of gladness above Your companions."
58_1_10: And, "In the beginning, O Lord, You laid the foundation of the earth — and the heavens are the works of Your hands.
58_1_11: They will perish, but You remain — and they all will become old like a garment;
58_1_12: and like a robe You will roll them up; like a garment they will also be changed. But You are the same — and Your years will not come to an end."
58_1_13: But to which of the angels has He ever said, "Sit at My right hand, until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet"?
58_1_14: Are they not all ministering spirits — sent out to render service for the sake of those who will inherit salvation?
58_2_1: For this reason we must pay much closer attention to what we have heard — so that we do not drift away from it.
58_2_2: For if the word spoken through angels proved unalterable, and every transgression and disobedience received a just penalty,
58_2_3: how will we escape if we neglect so great a salvation? — which at the first was spoken through the Lord, and was confirmed to us by those who heard,
58_2_4: while God also testified along with them — both by signs and wonders, and by various miracles, and by gifts of the Holy Spirit, distributed according to His will.
58_2_5: For He did not subject to angels the world to come — concerning which we are speaking.
58_2_6: But one has testified somewhere, saying, "What is man, that You remember him? Or the son of man, that You are concerned about him?
58_2_7: You made him for a little while lower than the angels. You crowned him with glory and honor — and appointed him over the works of Your hands.
58_2_8: You have put all things in subjection under his feet." For in subjecting all things to him, He left nothing that is not subject to him. But now we do not yet see all things subjected to him.
58_2_9: But we do see Him — Jesus, who was made for a little while lower than the angels — namely, Jesus, because of the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honor; so that by the grace of God, He might taste death for everyone.
58_2_10: For it was fitting for Him — for whom are all things, and through whom are all things — in bringing many sons to glory, to perfect the author of their salvation through sufferings.
58_2_11: For both He who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are all from one Father — for which reason He is not ashamed to call them brothers,
58_2_12: saying, "I will declare Your name to My brothers — in the midst of the assembly I will sing Your praise."
58_2_13: And again, "I will put My trust in Him." And again, "Behold, I and the children whom God has given Me."
58_2_14: Therefore, since the children share in flesh and blood — He Himself likewise also partook of the same — so that through death He might render powerless him who had the power of death, that is, the devil.
58_2_15: And free those who through fear of death were subject to slavery all their lives.
58_2_16: For assuredly He does not give help to angels — but He gives help to the descendants of Abraham.
58_2_17: Therefore He had to be made like His brothers in all things — so that He might become a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make propitiation for the sins of the people.
58_2_18: For since He Himself was tempted in that which He has suffered — He is able to come to the aid of those who are tempted.
58_3_1: Therefore, holy brothers — partakers of a heavenly calling — consider Jesus, the Apostle and High Priest of our confession.
58_3_2: He was faithful to Him who appointed Him — as Moses also was in all His house.
58_3_3: For He has been counted worthy of more glory than Moses, by just so much as the builder of the house has more honor than the house.
58_3_4: For every house is built by someone — but the builder of all things is God.
58_3_5: And Moses was faithful in all God's house, as a servant — for a testimony of those things which were to be spoken later.
58_3_6: But Christ was faithful as a Son over His house — whose house we are, if we hold fast our confidence and the boast of our hope firm until the end.
58_3_7: Therefore, just as the Holy Spirit says: "Today, if you hear His voice,
58_3_8: do not harden your hearts as when they provoked Me — as in the day of trial in the wilderness,
58_3_9: where your fathers tried Me by testing Me — and saw My works for forty years.
58_3_10: Therefore I was angry with this generation — and said, 'They always go astray in their heart, and they did not know My ways.'
58_3_11: As I swore in My wrath: 'They shall not enter My rest.'"
58_3_12: Take care, brothers, that there not be in any one of you an evil, unbelieving heart that falls away from the living God.
58_3_13: But encourage one another day after day — as long as it is still called "Today" — so that none of you will be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
58_3_14: For we have become partakers of Christ — if we hold fast the beginning of our assurance firm until the end.
58_3_15: While it is said, "Today if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts, as when they provoked Me."
58_3_16: For who provoked Him when they had heard? Indeed, was it not all those who came out of Egypt led by Moses?
58_3_17: And with whom was He angry for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned — whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
58_3_18: And to whom did He swear that they would not enter His rest, but to those who were disobedient?
58_3_19: So we see that they were not able to enter because of unbelief.
58_4_1: Therefore, let us fear if, while a promise remains of entering His rest, any one of you may seem to have come short of it.
58_4_2: For indeed we have had good news preached to us, just as they also did. But the word they heard did not profit them — because it was not united by faith in those who heard.
58_4_3: For we who have believed enter that rest — just as He has said, "As I swore in My wrath, they shall not enter My rest" — although His works were finished from the foundation of the world.
58_4_4: For He has said somewhere concerning the seventh day: "And God rested on the seventh day from all His works."
58_4_5: And again in this passage, "They shall not enter My rest."
58_4_6: Therefore, since it remains for some to enter it — and those who formerly had good news preached to them did not enter because of disobedience —
58_4_7: He again fixes a certain day, "Today," saying through David — after so long a time — just as has been said before: "Today if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts."
58_4_8: For if Joshua had given them rest, He would not have spoken of another day after that.
58_4_9: So there remains a Sabbath rest for the people of God.
58_4_10: For the one who has entered His rest has himself also rested from his works — as God did from His.
58_4_11: Therefore let us be diligent to enter that rest — so that no one will fall by following the same example of disobedience.
58_4_12: For the word of God is living and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword — piercing as far as the division of soul and spirit, of both joints and marrow — and able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
58_4_13: And there is no creature hidden from His sight — but all things are open and laid bare to the eyes of Him with whom we have to do.
58_4_14: Therefore, since we have a great High Priest who has passed through the heavens — Jesus the Son of God — let us hold fast our confession.
58_4_15: For we do not have a High Priest who cannot sympathize with our weaknesses — but One who has been tempted in all things as we are, yet without sin.
58_4_16: Therefore let us draw near with confidence to the throne of grace — so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need.
58_5_1: For every high priest taken from among men is appointed on behalf of men in things pertaining to God — to offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins.
58_5_2: He can deal gently with the ignorant and misguided — since he himself also is beset with weakness.
58_5_3: And because of it, he is obligated to offer sacrifices for sins, as for the people, so also for himself.
58_5_4: And no one takes the honor to himself — but he receives it when he is called by God, even as Aaron was.
58_5_5: So also Christ did not glorify Himself so as to become a high priest — but He who said to Him, "You are My Son; today I have begotten You."
58_5_6: Just as He says also in another passage, "You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek."
58_5_7: In the days of His flesh, He offered up both prayers and supplications, with loud crying and tears, to the One able to save Him from death — and He was heard because of His piety.
58_5_8: Although He was a Son, He learned obedience from the things which He suffered.
58_5_9: And having been made perfect, He became to all those who obey Him the source of eternal salvation —
58_5_10: being designated by God as a high priest according to the order of Melchizedek.
58_5_11: Concerning him we have much to say — and it is hard to explain, since you have become dull of hearing.
58_5_12: For though by this time you ought to be teachers, you have need again for someone to teach you the elementary principles of the oracles of God. And you have come to need milk and not solid food.
58_5_13: For everyone who partakes only of milk is unaccustomed to the word of righteousness — for he is an infant.
58_5_14: But solid food is for the mature — who because of practice have their senses trained to discern good and evil.
58_6_1: Therefore leaving the elementary teaching about the Christ, let us press on to maturity — not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God,
58_6_2: of instruction about washings, and laying on of hands, and the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.
58_6_3: And this we will do, if God permits.
58_6_4: For in the case of those who have once been enlightened — and have tasted the heavenly gift, and have been made partakers of the Holy Spirit,
58_6_5: and have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the age to come,
58_6_6: and then have fallen away — it is impossible to renew them again to repentance, since they again crucify to themselves the Son of God, and put Him to open shame.
58_6_7: For ground that drinks the rain which often falls on it, and brings forth vegetation useful to those for whose sake it is also tilled — receives a blessing from God.
58_6_8: But if it yields thorns and thistles, it is worthless and close to being cursed — and it ends up being burned.
58_6_9: But, beloved, we are convinced of better things concerning you — and things that accompany salvation, though we are speaking in this way.
58_6_10: For God is not unjust so as to forget your work and the love which you have shown toward His name — in having ministered to the saints, and in still ministering.
58_6_11: And we desire that each one of you show the same diligence — so as to realize the full assurance of hope until the end.
58_6_12: So that you will not be sluggish — but imitators of those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
58_6_13: For when God made the promise to Abraham — since He could swear by no one greater, He swore by Himself,
58_6_14: saying, "I will surely bless you, and I will surely multiply you."
58_6_15: And so, having patiently waited, he obtained the promise.
58_6_16: For men swear by one greater than themselves — and with them an oath given as confirmation is an end of every dispute.
58_6_17: In the same way, God, desiring even more to show to the heirs of the promise the unchangeableness of His purpose, interposed with an oath —
58_6_18: so that by two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have taken refuge would have strong encouragement to take hold of the hope set before us.
58_6_19: This hope we have as an anchor of the soul — both sure and steadfast, and one which enters within the veil,
58_6_20: where Jesus has entered as a forerunner for us — having become a high priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.
58_7_1: For this Melchizedek — king of Salem, priest of the Most High God — who met Abraham as he was returning from the slaughter of the kings, and blessed him,
58_7_2: to whom Abraham also apportioned a tenth of all the spoils — was first of all, by translation of his name, king of righteousness; and then also king of Salem, which is king of peace.
58_7_3: Without father, without mother, without genealogy — having neither beginning of days nor end of life — but made like the Son of God, he remains a priest perpetually.
58_7_4: Now observe how great this man was, to whom Abraham, the patriarch, gave a tenth of the choicest spoils.
58_7_5: And those indeed of the sons of Levi who receive the priest's office have commandment in the Law to collect a tenth from the people — that is, from their brothers, although these are descended from Abraham.
58_7_6: But the one whose genealogy is not traced from them collected a tenth from Abraham — and blessed the one who had the promises.
58_7_7: But without any dispute, the lesser is blessed by the greater.
58_7_8: And in this case mortal men receive tithes — but in that case, one receives them, of whom it is witnessed that he lives on.
58_7_9: And, so to speak, through Abraham even Levi — who received tithes — paid tithes,
58_7_10: for he was still in the loins of his father when Melchizedek met him.
58_7_11: Now if perfection had been through the Levitical priesthood — for on the basis of it the people received the Law — what further need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not be designated according to the order of Aaron?
58_7_12: For when the priesthood is changed, of necessity there takes place a change of law also.
58_7_13: For the One concerning whom these things are spoken belongs to another tribe — from which no one has officiated at the altar.
58_7_14: For it is evident that our Lord was descended from Judah — a tribe with reference to which Moses spoke nothing concerning priests.
58_7_15: And this is clearer still — if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
58_7_16: who has become such not on the basis of a law of physical requirement — but according to the power of an indestructible life.
58_7_17: For it is attested of Him, "You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek."
58_7_18: For, on the one hand, there is a setting aside of a former commandment — because of its weakness and uselessness
58_7_19: (for the Law made nothing perfect) — and on the other hand, there is the bringing in of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
58_7_20: And inasmuch as it was not without an oath
58_7_21: (for they indeed became priests without an oath, but He with an oath through the One who said to Him: "The Lord has sworn, and will not change His mind: 'You are a priest forever' ") —
58_7_22: so much the more also, Jesus has become the guarantee of a better covenant.
58_7_23: And the former priests, on the one hand, existed in greater numbers because they were prevented by death from continuing.
58_7_24: But Jesus, on the other hand, because He continues forever, holds His priesthood permanently.
58_7_25: Therefore He is able also to save forever those who draw near to God through Him — since He always lives to make intercession for them.
58_7_26: For it was fitting for us to have such a high priest — holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and exalted above the heavens.
58_7_27: Who does not need daily, like those high priests, to offer up sacrifices, first for His own sins, and then for the sins of the people — because this He did once for all when He offered up Himself.
58_7_28: For the Law appoints men as high priests who are weak — but the word of the oath, which came after the Law, appoints a Son, made perfect forever.
58_8_1: Now the main point in what has been said is this: we have such a high priest — One who has taken His seat at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,
58_8_2: a minister in the sanctuary and in the true tabernacle — which the Lord pitched, not man.
58_8_3: For every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices — therefore it is necessary that this priest also have something to offer.
58_8_4: Now if He were on earth, He would not be a priest at all — since there are those who offer the gifts according to the Law,
58_8_5: who serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things. As Moses was warned by God when he was about to erect the tabernacle: "See," He says, "that you make all things according to the pattern which was shown you on the mountain."
58_8_6: But now He has obtained a more excellent ministry — by as much as He is also the mediator of a better covenant, which has been enacted on better promises.
58_8_7: For if that first covenant had been faultless, there would have been no occasion sought for a second.
58_8_8: For finding fault with them, He says: "Behold, days are coming, says the Lord — when I will effect a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.
58_8_9: Not like the covenant which I made with their fathers — on the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt. For they did not continue in My covenant, and I did not care for them, says the Lord.
58_8_10: For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put My laws into their minds, and I will write them on their hearts. And I will be their God, and they shall be My people.
58_8_11: And they shall not teach everyone his fellow citizen, and everyone his brother, saying, 'Know the Lord' — for all will know Me, from the least to the greatest of them.
58_8_12: For I will be merciful to their iniquities, and I will remember their sins no more."
58_8_13: When He said, "A new covenant," He has made the first obsolete. But whatever is becoming obsolete and growing old is ready to disappear.
58_9_1: Now even the first covenant had regulations of divine worship and the earthly sanctuary.
58_9_2: For there was a tabernacle prepared — the outer one — in which were the lampstand, and the table, and the consecrated bread; this is called the holy place.
58_9_3: And behind the second veil there was a tabernacle, which is called the Holy of Holies —
58_9_4: having a golden altar of incense, and the ark of the covenant covered on all sides with gold; in which was a golden jar holding the manna, and Aaron's rod which budded, and the tablets of the covenant.
58_9_5: And above it were the cherubim of glory, overshadowing the mercy seat — but of these things we cannot now speak in detail.
58_9_6: Now when these things have been so prepared, the priests are continually entering the outer tabernacle, performing the divine worship.
58_9_7: But into the second, only the high priest enters — once a year, not without taking blood, which he offers for himself, and for the sins of the people committed in ignorance.
58_9_8: The Holy Spirit is signifying this: that the way into the holy place has not yet been disclosed — while the outer tabernacle is still standing.
58_9_9: Which is a symbol for the present time — according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered, which cannot make the worshiper perfect in conscience —
58_9_10: since they relate only to food and drink and various washings — regulations for the body imposed until a time of reformation.
58_9_11: But when Christ appeared as a high priest of the good things to come — He entered through the greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is, not of this creation;
58_9_12: and not through the blood of goats and calves, but through His own blood — He entered the holy place once for all, having obtained eternal redemption.
58_9_13: For if the blood of goats and bulls — and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled — sanctify for the cleansing of the flesh,
58_9_14: how much more will the blood of Christ — who through the eternal Spirit offered Himself without blemish to God — cleanse your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?
58_9_15: And for this reason He is the mediator of a new covenant — so that, since a death has taken place for the redemption of the transgressions that were committed under the first covenant, those who have been called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.
58_9_16: For where a covenant is, there must of necessity be the death of the one who made it.
58_9_17: For a covenant is valid only when men are dead — for it is never in force while the one who made it lives.
58_9_18: Therefore, even the first covenant was not inaugurated without blood.
58_9_19: For when every commandment had been spoken by Moses to all the people according to the Law, he took the blood of calves and goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop — and sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,
58_9_20: saying, "This is the blood of the covenant which God commanded you."
58_9_21: And in the same way he sprinkled both the tabernacle and all the vessels of the ministry with the blood.
58_9_22: And according to the Law, one may almost say all things are cleansed with blood — and without shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.
58_9_23: Therefore it was necessary for the copies of the things in the heavens to be cleansed with these — but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
58_9_24: For Christ did not enter a holy place made with hands — a mere copy of the true one — but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us.
58_9_25: Nor was it that He would offer Himself often — as the high priest enters the holy place year by year with blood that is not his own.
58_9_26: Otherwise He would have needed to suffer often since the foundation of the world. But now once at the consummation of the ages, He has been manifested to put away sin by the sacrifice of Himself.
58_9_27: And inasmuch as it is appointed for men to die once — and after this comes judgment —
58_9_28: so Christ also, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time for salvation, without reference to sin, to those who eagerly await Him.
58_10_1: For the Law, since it has only a shadow of the good things to come, and not the very form of things — can never, by the same sacrifices which they offer continually year by year, make perfect those who draw near.
58_10_2: Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered? — because the worshipers, having once been cleansed, would no longer have had consciousness of sins.
58_10_3: But in those sacrifices there is a reminder of sins year by year.
58_10_4: For it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
58_10_5: Therefore, when He comes into the world, He says: "Sacrifice and offering You have not desired — but a body You have prepared for Me.
58_10_6: In whole burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin You have taken no pleasure.
58_10_7: Then I said, 'Behold, I have come (in the scroll of the book it is written of Me) to do Your will, O God.'"
58_10_8: After saying above, "Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin You have not desired — nor have You taken pleasure in them" (which are offered according to the Law),
58_10_9: then He said, "Behold, I have come to do Your will." He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
58_10_10: By this will we have been sanctified — through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
58_10_11: And every priest stands daily ministering and offering time after time the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.
58_10_12: But He, having offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, sat down at the right hand of God —
58_10_13: from then on waiting until His enemies are made a footstool for His feet.
58_10_14: For by one offering He has perfected for all time those who are sanctified.
58_10_15: And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us. For after saying,
58_10_16: "This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: I will put My laws upon their hearts, and on their mind I will write them."
58_10_17: He then says, "And their sins and their lawless deeds I will remember no more."
58_10_18: Now where there is forgiveness of these things, there is no longer any offering for sin.
58_10_19: Therefore, brothers — since we have confidence to enter the holy place by the blood of Jesus,
58_10_20: by a new and living way which He inaugurated for us through the veil — that is, His flesh —
58_10_21: and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
58_10_22: let us draw near with a sincere heart, in full assurance of faith — having our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water.
58_10_23: Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering — for He who promised is faithful.
58_10_24: And let us consider how to stir up one another to love and good deeds —
58_10_25: not forsaking our own assembling together, as is the habit of some — but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the day drawing near.
58_10_26: For if we go on sinning willfully after receiving the knowledge of the truth, there no longer remains a sacrifice for sins —
58_10_27: but a terrifying expectation of judgment, and the fury of a fire which will consume the adversaries.
58_10_28: Anyone who has set aside the Law of Moses dies without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
58_10_29: How much severer punishment do you think he will deserve who has trampled underfoot the Son of God — and has regarded as unclean the blood of the covenant by which he was sanctified — and has insulted the Spirit of grace?
58_10_30: For we know Him who said, "Vengeance is Mine — I will repay." And again, "The Lord will judge His people."
58_10_31: It is a terrifying thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
58_10_32: But remember the former days, when, after being enlightened, you endured a great conflict of sufferings.
58_10_33: Partly by being made a public spectacle through reproaches and tribulations — and partly by becoming sharers with those who were so treated.
58_10_34: For you showed sympathy to the prisoners — and accepted joyfully the seizure of your property — knowing that you have for yourselves a better and lasting possession.
58_10_35: Therefore, do not throw away your confidence — which has a great reward.
58_10_36: For you have need of endurance, so that when you have done the will of God, you may receive what was promised.
58_10_37: For yet in a very little while, He who is coming will come, and will not delay.
58_10_38: But My righteous one shall live by faith. And if he shrinks back, My soul has no pleasure in him.
58_10_39: But we are not of those who shrink back to destruction — but of those who have faith to the preserving of the soul.
58_11_1: Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for — the conviction of things not seen.
58_11_2: For by it the men of old gained approval.
58_11_3: By faith we understand that the worlds were prepared by the word of God — so that what is seen was not made out of things which are visible.
58_11_4: By faith Abel offered to God a better sacrifice than Cain — through which he was attested to be righteous; God testifying about his gifts. And through faith, though he is dead, he still speaks.
58_11_5: By faith Enoch was taken up — so that he would not see death; and he was not found, because God took him up. For he obtained the witness, before his being taken up, that he was pleasing to God.
58_11_6: And without faith it is impossible to please Him — for he who comes to God must believe that He is, and that He is a rewarder of those who seek Him.
58_11_7: By faith Noah, being warned by God about things not yet seen — in reverence prepared an ark for the salvation of his household. By this he condemned the world, and became an heir of the righteousness which is according to faith.
58_11_8: By faith Abraham, when he was called, obeyed by going out to a place which he was to receive for an inheritance — and he went out, not knowing where he was going.
58_11_9: By faith he lived as an alien in the land of promise, as in a foreign land — dwelling in tents with Isaac and Jacob, fellow heirs of the same promise.
58_11_10: For he was looking for the city which has foundations — whose architect and builder is God.
58_11_11: By faith even Sarah herself received ability to conceive, even beyond the proper time of life — since she considered Him faithful who had promised.
58_11_12: Therefore, also from one man — and him as good as dead at that — there were born descendants as many as the stars of heaven in number, and innumerable as the sand which is by the seashore.
58_11_13: All these died in faith, without receiving the promises — but having seen them and welcomed them from a distance, and having confessed that they were strangers and exiles on the earth.
58_11_14: For those who say such things make it clear that they are seeking a country of their own.
58_11_15: And indeed if they had been thinking of that country from which they went out, they would have had opportunity to return.
58_11_16: But as it is, they desire a better country — that is, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed to be called their God — for He has prepared a city for them.
58_11_17: By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac — and he who had received the promises was offering up his only begotten son.
58_11_18: It was he to whom it was said, "In Isaac your descendants shall be called."
58_11_19: He considered that God is able to raise people even from the dead — from which he also received him back as a type.
58_11_20: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau, even regarding things to come.
58_11_21: By faith Jacob, as he was dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph — and worshiped, leaning on the top of his staff.
58_11_22: By faith Joseph, when he was dying, made mention of the exodus of the sons of Israel, and gave orders concerning his bones.
58_11_23: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents — because they saw he was a beautiful child; and they were not afraid of the king's edict.
58_11_24: By faith Moses, when he had grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter —
58_11_25: choosing rather to endure ill-treatment with the people of God, than to enjoy the passing pleasures of sin.
58_11_26: Considering the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures of Egypt — for he was looking to the reward.
58_11_27: By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king — for he endured, as seeing Him who is unseen.
58_11_28: By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood — so that he who destroyed the firstborn would not touch them.
58_11_29: By faith they passed through the Red Sea as on dry land — and the Egyptians, when they attempted it, were drowned.
58_11_30: By faith the walls of Jericho fell down, after they had been encircled for seven days.
58_11_31: By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish along with those who were disobedient — after she had welcomed the spies in peace.
58_11_32: And what more shall I say? For time will fail me if I tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, of David and Samuel, and the prophets —
58_11_33: who by faith conquered kingdoms, performed acts of righteousness, obtained promises, shut the mouths of lions,
58_11_34: quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword. From weakness they were made strong; they became mighty in war, put foreign armies to flight.
58_11_35: Women received back their dead by resurrection. And others were tortured, not accepting their release — so that they might obtain a better resurrection.
58_11_36: And others experienced mockings and scourgings, and even chains and imprisonment.
58_11_37: They were stoned, they were sawn in two, they were tempted, they were put to death with the sword. They went about in sheepskins, in goatskins, being destitute, afflicted, ill-treated —
58_11_38: men of whom the world was not worthy. Wandering in deserts and mountains, and in caves and holes in the ground.
58_11_39: And all these, having gained approval through their faith, did not receive what was promised —
58_11_40: because God had provided something better for us, so that apart from us they would not be made perfect.
58_12_1: Therefore, since we have so great a cloud of witnesses surrounding us — let us also lay aside every encumbrance and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let us run with endurance the race that is set before us,
58_12_2: fixing our eyes on Jesus — the author and perfecter of faith — who, for the joy set before Him, endured the cross, despising the shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
58_12_3: For consider Him who has endured such hostility by sinners against Himself — so that you will not grow weary and lose heart.
58_12_4: You have not yet resisted to the point of bloodshed in your striving against sin.
58_12_5: And you have forgotten the exhortation which is addressed to you as sons: "My son, do not regard lightly the discipline of the Lord — nor faint when you are reproved by Him.
58_12_6: For those whom the Lord loves, He disciplines — and He scourges every son whom He receives."
58_12_7: It is for discipline that you endure. God deals with you as with sons — for what son is there whom his father does not discipline?
58_12_8: But if you are without discipline — of which all have become partakers — then you are illegitimate children, and not sons.
58_12_9: Furthermore, we had earthly fathers to discipline us, and we respected them — shall we not much rather be subject to the Father of spirits, and live?
58_12_10: For they disciplined us for a short time as seemed best to them — but He disciplines us for our good, so that we may share His holiness.
58_12_11: All discipline for the moment seems not to be joyful, but sorrowful — yet to those who have been trained by it, afterwards it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness.
58_12_12: Therefore, strengthen the hands that are weak and the knees that are feeble.
58_12_13: And make straight paths for your feet — so that the limb which is lame may not be put out of joint, but rather be healed.
58_12_14: Pursue peace with all men — and the sanctification without which no one will see the Lord.
58_12_15: See to it that no one comes short of the grace of God — that no root of bitterness springing up causes trouble, and by it many be defiled.
58_12_16: That there be no immoral or godless person like Esau, who sold his own birthright for a single meal.
58_12_17: For you know that even afterwards, when he desired to inherit the blessing, he was rejected — for he found no place for repentance, though he sought for it with tears.
58_12_18: For you have not come to a mountain that can be touched, and to a blazing fire — and to darkness and gloom and whirlwind,
58_12_19: and to the blast of a trumpet and the sound of words — which sound was such that those who heard begged that no further word be spoken to them.
58_12_20: For they could not bear the command, "If even a beast touches the mountain, it will be stoned."
58_12_21: And so terrible was the sight, that Moses said, "I am full of fear and trembling."
58_12_22: But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God — the heavenly Jerusalem — and to myriads of angels in festal assembly,
58_12_23: and to the church of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven, and to God, the Judge of all, and to the spirits of the righteous made perfect,
58_12_24: and to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant — and to the sprinkled blood, which speaks better than the blood of Abel.
58_12_25: See to it that you do not refuse Him who is speaking. For if those did not escape when they refused him who warned them on earth, much less will we escape who turn away from Him who warns from heaven.
58_12_26: And His voice shook the earth then. But now He has promised, saying, "Yet once more I will shake not only the earth, but also the heavens."
58_12_27: And this expression, "Yet once more," denotes the removing of those things which can be shaken, as of created things — so that those things which cannot be shaken may remain.
58_12_28: Therefore, since we receive a kingdom which cannot be shaken — let us show gratitude, by which we may offer to God an acceptable service with reverence and awe.
58_12_29: For our God is a consuming fire.
58_13_1: Let love of the brothers continue.
58_13_2: Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers — for by this some have entertained angels without knowing it.
58_13_3: Remember the prisoners, as though in prison with them — and those who are ill-treated, since you yourselves also are in the body.
58_13_4: Marriage is to be held in honor among all — and the marriage bed is to be undefiled. For fornicators and adulterers God will judge.
58_13_5: Make sure that your character is free from the love of money. Be content with what you have — for He Himself has said, "I will never desert you, nor will I ever forsake you."
58_13_6: So that we confidently say, "The Lord is my helper — I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?"
58_13_7: Remember those who led you — who spoke the word of God to you. And considering the result of their conduct, imitate their faith.
58_13_8: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today — and forever.
58_13_9: Do not be carried away by varied and strange teachings. For it is good for the heart to be strengthened by grace — not by foods, through which those who were so occupied were not benefited.
58_13_10: We have an altar from which those who serve the tabernacle have no right to eat.
58_13_11: For the bodies of those animals whose blood is brought into the holy place by the high priest as an offering for sin, are burned outside the camp.
58_13_12: Therefore Jesus also — that He might sanctify the people through His own blood — suffered outside the gate.
58_13_13: So, let us go out to Him outside the camp — bearing His reproach.
58_13_14: For here we do not have a lasting city — but we are seeking the city which is to come.
58_13_15: Through Him then, let us continually offer up a sacrifice of praise to God — that is, the fruit of lips that give thanks to His name.
58_13_16: And do not neglect doing good and sharing — for with such sacrifices God is pleased.
58_13_17: Obey your leaders, and submit to them — for they keep watch over your souls, as those who will give an account. Let them do this with joy and not with grief — for this would be unprofitable for you.
58_13_18: Pray for us. For we are sure that we have a good conscience — desiring to conduct ourselves honorably in all things.
58_13_19: And I urge you all the more to do this — so that I may be restored to you the sooner.
58_13_20: Now the God of peace, who brought up from the dead the great Shepherd of the sheep through the blood of the eternal covenant — that is, Jesus our Lord —
58_13_21: equip you in every good thing to do His will — working in us that which is pleasing in His sight, through Jesus Christ. To Him be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
58_13_22: But I urge you, brothers — bear with this word of exhortation, for I have written to you briefly.
58_13_23: Take notice that our brother Timothy has been released — with whom, if he comes soon, I will see you.
58_13_24: Greet all of your leaders, and all the saints. Those from Italy greet you.
58_13_25: Grace be with you all. Amen.
45_1_1: Paul, a bondservant of Christ Jesus — called as an apostle, set apart for the gospel of God,
45_1_2: which He promised beforehand through His prophets in the holy Scriptures —
45_1_3: concerning His Son — who was born of a descendant of David according to the flesh,
45_1_4: who was declared the Son of God with power, by the resurrection from the dead, according to the Spirit of holiness — Jesus Christ our Lord.
45_1_5: Through Him we have received grace and apostleship — to bring about the obedience of faith among all the Gentiles, for His name's sake.
45_1_6: Among them you also are the called of Jesus Christ.
45_1_7: To all who are beloved of God in Rome, called as saints: Grace to you, and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
45_1_8: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all — because your faith is being proclaimed throughout the whole world.
45_1_9: For God, whom I serve in my spirit in the preaching of the gospel of His Son, is my witness — as to how unceasingly I make mention of you,
45_1_10: always in my prayers — making request, if perhaps now at last, by the will of God, I may succeed in coming to you.
45_1_11: For I long to see you — so that I may impart some spiritual gift to you, that you may be established;
45_1_12: that is, that I may be encouraged together with you while among you — each of us by the other's faith, both yours and mine.
45_1_13: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that often I have planned to come to you (and have been prevented so far) — so that I may obtain some fruit among you also, even as among the rest of the Gentiles.
45_1_14: I am under obligation both to Greeks and to barbarians, both to the wise and to the foolish.
45_1_15: So, for my part, I am eager to preach the gospel to you also, who are in Rome.
45_1_16: For I am not ashamed of the gospel — for it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.
45_1_17: For in it the righteousness of God is revealed — from faith to faith. As it is written: "But the righteous man shall live by faith."
45_1_18: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven, against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who suppress the truth in unrighteousness —
45_1_19: because that which is known about God is evident within them — for God made it evident to them.
45_1_20: For since the creation of the world His invisible attributes — His eternal power and divine nature — have been clearly seen, being understood through what has been made. So they are without excuse.
45_1_21: For even though they knew God, they did not honor Him as God, or give thanks. But they became futile in their thinking, and their foolish heart was darkened.
45_1_22: Professing to be wise, they became fools.
45_1_23: And exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for an image in the form of corruptible man, and of birds, and four-footed animals, and crawling creatures.
45_1_24: Therefore God gave them over in the lusts of their hearts to impurity — that their bodies would be dishonored among them.
45_1_25: For they exchanged the truth of God for a lie — and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.
45_1_26: For this reason God gave them over to degrading passions. For their women exchanged the natural function for that which is unnatural.
45_1_27: And in the same way also the men abandoned the natural function of the woman — and burned in their desire toward one another, men with men committing indecent acts, and receiving in their own persons the due penalty of their error.
45_1_28: And just as they did not see fit to acknowledge God any longer, God gave them over to a depraved mind — to do those things which are not proper.
45_1_29: Being filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, greed, and evil — full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, malice. They are gossips,
45_1_30: slanderers, haters of God, insolent, arrogant, boastful, inventors of evil, disobedient to parents,
45_1_32: And although they know the ordinance of God — that those who practice such things are worthy of death — they not only do the same, but also give hearty approval to those who practice them.
45_2_1: Therefore you have no excuse, O man — every one of you who passes judgment. For in that which you judge another, you condemn yourself — for you who judge practice the same things.
45_2_2: And we know that the judgment of God rightly falls upon those who practice such things.
45_2_3: But do you suppose this, O man — when you pass judgment on those who practice such things, and yet do the same yourself — that you will escape the judgment of God?
45_2_4: Or do you think lightly of the riches of His kindness and tolerance and patience? — not knowing that the kindness of God leads you to repentance.
45_2_5: But because of your stubbornness and unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath for yourself in the day of wrath — and the revelation of the righteous judgment of God,
45_2_6: who will render to each person according to his deeds:
45_2_7: to those who by perseverance in doing good seek for glory and honor and immortality — eternal life;
45_2_8: but to those who are selfishly ambitious — and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness — wrath and indignation.
45_2_9: There will be tribulation and distress for every soul of man who does evil — of the Jew first, and also of the Greek.
45_2_10: But glory and honor and peace to everyone who does good — to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.
45_2_11: For there is no partiality with God.
45_2_12: For all who have sinned without the Law will also perish without the Law — and all who have sinned under the Law will be judged by the Law.
45_2_13: For it is not the hearers of the Law who are righteous before God — but the doers of the Law will be justified.
45_2_14: For when Gentiles, who do not have the Law, instinctively do the things of the Law — these, not having the Law, are a law to themselves.
45_2_15: In that they show the work of the Law written in their hearts — their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts alternately accusing or defending them —
45_2_16: on the day when, according to my gospel, God will judge the secrets of men through Christ Jesus.
45_2_17: But if you bear the name "Jew" — and rely upon the Law, and boast in God,
45_2_18: and know His will, and approve the things that are essential, being instructed out of the Law,
45_2_19: and are confident that you yourself are a guide to the blind, a light to those in darkness,
45_2_20: a corrector of the foolish, a teacher of the immature — having in the Law the embodiment of knowledge and of the truth —
45_2_21: you, therefore, who teach another — do you not teach yourself? You who preach that one shall not steal — do you steal?
45_2_22: You who say that one should not commit adultery — do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols — do you rob temples?
45_2_23: You who boast in the Law — through your breaking the Law, do you dishonor God?
45_2_24: For "the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you" — just as it is written.
45_2_25: For circumcision is indeed of value if you practice the Law — but if you are a transgressor of the Law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
45_2_26: So if the uncircumcised man keeps the requirements of the Law — will not his uncircumcision be regarded as circumcision?
45_2_27: And he who is physically uncircumcised, if he keeps the Law, will he not judge you — who though having the letter of the Law and circumcision are a transgressor of the Law?
45_2_28: For he is not a Jew who is one outwardly — nor is circumcision that which is outward in the flesh.
45_2_29: But he is a Jew who is one inwardly — and circumcision is that which is of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the letter; and his praise is not from men, but from God.
45_3_1: Then what advantage has the Jew? — or what is the benefit of circumcision?
45_3_2: Great in every respect. First of all, that they were entrusted with the oracles of God.
45_3_3: What then? If some did not believe, their unbelief will not nullify the faithfulness of God, will it?
45_3_4: May it never be! Rather, let God be found true, though every man be found a liar — as it is written: "That You may be justified in Your words, and prevail when You are judged."
45_3_5: But if our unrighteousness demonstrates the righteousness of God, what shall we say? The God who inflicts wrath is not unrighteous, is He? (I am speaking in human terms.)
45_3_6: May it never be! For otherwise, how will God judge the world?
45_3_7: But if through my lie the truth of God abounded to His glory, why am I also still being judged as a sinner?
45_3_8: And why not say (as we are slanderously reported and as some claim that we say), "Let us do evil that good may come"? Their condemnation is just.
45_3_9: What then? Are we better than they? Not at all! For we have already charged that both Jews and Greeks are all under sin.
45_3_10: As it is written: "There is none righteous — not even one.
45_3_11: There is none who understands; there is none who seeks for God.
45_3_12: All have turned aside; together they have become useless. There is none who does good — there is not even one."
45_3_13: "Their throat is an open grave; with their tongues they keep deceiving." "The poison of asps is under their lips."
45_3_14: "Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness."
45_3_15: "Their feet are swift to shed blood.
45_3_16: Destruction and misery are in their paths.
45_3_17: And the path of peace they have not known."
45_3_18: "There is no fear of God before their eyes."
45_3_19: Now we know that whatever the Law says, it speaks to those who are under the Law — so that every mouth may be closed, and all the world may become accountable to God.
45_3_20: Because by the works of the Law no flesh will be justified in His sight — for through the Law comes the knowledge of sin.
45_3_21: But now apart from the Law, the righteousness of God has been manifested — being witnessed by the Law and the Prophets;
45_3_22: even the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ — for all those who believe. For there is no distinction.
45_3_23: For all have sinned, and fall short of the glory of God —
45_3_24: being justified as a gift by His grace, through the redemption which is in Christ Jesus.
45_3_25: Whom God displayed publicly as a propitiation in His blood through faith — this was to demonstrate His righteousness, because in the forbearance of God, He passed over the sins previously committed.
45_3_26: For the demonstration, I say, of His righteousness at the present time — so that He would be just, and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus.
45_3_27: Where then is boasting? It is excluded. By what kind of law? Of works? No, but by a law of faith.
45_3_28: For we maintain that a man is justified by faith — apart from works of the Law.
45_3_29: Or is God the God of Jews only? Is He not the God of Gentiles also? Yes — of Gentiles also.
45_3_30: Since indeed God who will justify the circumcised by faith, and the uncircumcised through faith, is one.
45_3_31: Do we then nullify the Law through faith? May it never be! On the contrary — we establish the Law.
45_4_1: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh, has found?
45_4_2: For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast about — but not before God.
45_4_3: For what does the Scripture say? "Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness."
45_4_4: Now to the one who works, his wage is not credited as a favor — but as what is due.
45_4_5: But to the one who does not work, but believes in Him who justifies the ungodly — his faith is credited as righteousness.
45_4_6: Just as David also speaks of the blessing on the man to whom God credits righteousness apart from works:
45_4_7: "Blessed are those whose lawless deeds have been forgiven, and whose sins have been covered.
45_4_8: Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will not take into account."
45_4_9: Is this blessing then on the circumcised, or on the uncircumcised also? For we say, "Faith was credited to Abraham as righteousness."
45_4_10: How then was it credited? While he was circumcised, or uncircumcised? Not while circumcised — but while uncircumcised.
45_4_11: And he received the sign of circumcision — a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had while uncircumcised — so that he might be the father of all who believe without being circumcised, that righteousness might be credited to them,
45_4_12: and the father of circumcision to those who not only are of the circumcision, but who also follow in the steps of the faith of our father Abraham — which he had while uncircumcised.
45_4_13: For the promise to Abraham or to his descendants — that he would be heir of the world — was not through the Law, but through the righteousness of faith.
45_4_14: For if those who are of the Law are heirs, faith is made void, and the promise is nullified.
45_4_15: For the Law brings about wrath — but where there is no law, there also is no violation.
45_4_16: For this reason it is by faith — so that it may be in accordance with grace, in order that the promise may be guaranteed to all the descendants — not only to those who are of the Law, but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all.
45_4_17: (As it is written, "A father of many nations have I made you.") In the presence of Him whom he believed — even God, who gives life to the dead and calls into being that which does not exist.
45_4_18: In hope against hope he believed — so that he might become a father of many nations, according to that which had been spoken: "So shall your descendants be."
45_4_19: And without becoming weak in faith, he contemplated his own body now as good as dead — since he was about a hundred years old — and the deadness of Sarah's womb.
45_4_20: Yet, with respect to the promise of God, he did not waver in unbelief — but grew strong in faith, giving glory to God.
45_4_21: And being fully assured that what God had promised, He was able also to perform.
45_4_22: Therefore it was also credited to him as righteousness.
45_4_23: Now not for his sake only was it written that it was credited to him —
45_4_24: but for our sake also, to whom it will be credited — to those who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.
45_4_25: He who was delivered over because of our transgressions — and was raised because of our justification.
45_5_1: Therefore, having been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.
45_5_2: Through Him also we have obtained our introduction by faith into this grace in which we stand. And we exult in hope of the glory of God.
45_5_3: And not only this — but we also exult in our tribulations, knowing that tribulation brings about perseverance.
45_5_4: And perseverance, proven character; and proven character, hope.
45_5_5: And hope does not disappoint — because the love of God has been poured out within our hearts through the Holy Spirit, who was given to us.
45_5_6: For while we were still helpless, at the right time Christ died for the ungodly.
45_5_7: For one will hardly die for a righteous man — though perhaps for the good man someone would dare even to die.
45_5_8: But God demonstrates His own love toward us — in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
45_5_9: Much more then, having now been justified by His blood — we shall be saved from the wrath of God through Him.
45_5_10: For if while we were enemies we were reconciled to God through the death of His Son — much more, having been reconciled, we shall be saved by His life.
45_5_11: And not only this — but we also exult in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received the reconciliation.
45_5_12: Therefore, just as through one man sin entered into the world — and death through sin, and so death spread to all men, because all sinned —
45_5_13: for until the Law sin was in the world — but sin is not imputed when there is no law.
45_5_14: Nevertheless, death reigned from Adam until Moses — even over those who had not sinned in the likeness of the offense of Adam, who is a type of Him who was to come.
45_5_15: But the free gift is not like the transgression. For if by the transgression of the one the many died, much more did the grace of God and the gift by the grace of the one Man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many.
45_5_16: And the gift is not like that which came through the one who sinned. For on the one hand the judgment arose from one transgression, resulting in condemnation — but on the other hand, the free gift arose from many transgressions, resulting in justification.
45_5_17: For if by the transgression of the one, death reigned through the one — much more those who receive the abundance of grace, and of the gift of righteousness, will reign in life through the One — Jesus Christ.
45_5_18: So then, as through one transgression there resulted condemnation to all men — even so through one act of righteousness, there resulted justification of life to all men.
45_5_19: For as through the one man's disobedience the many were made sinners — even so through the obedience of the One, the many will be made righteous.
45_5_20: And the Law came in so that the transgression would increase. But where sin increased, grace abounded all the more.
45_5_21: So that as sin reigned in death — even so grace would reign through righteousness to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
45_6_1: What shall we say then? Are we to continue in sin so that grace may increase?
45_6_2: May it never be! How shall we who died to sin still live in it?
45_6_3: Or do you not know that all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus have been baptized into His death?
45_6_4: Therefore we have been buried with Him through baptism into death — so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we too might walk in newness of life.
45_6_5: For if we have become united with Him in the likeness of His death — certainly we shall also be in the likeness of His resurrection.
45_6_6: Knowing this — that our old self was crucified with Him, in order that our body of sin might be done away with, so that we would no longer be slaves to sin.
45_6_7: For he who has died is freed from sin.
45_6_8: Now if we have died with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with Him.
45_6_9: Knowing that Christ, having been raised from the dead, is never to die again — death no longer is master over Him.
45_6_10: For the death that He died, He died to sin once for all — but the life that He lives, He lives to God.
45_6_11: Even so, consider yourselves to be dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus.
45_6_12: Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body — so that you obey its lusts.
45_6_13: And do not go on presenting the members of your body to sin as instruments of unrighteousness — but present yourselves to God as those alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness to God.
45_6_14: For sin shall not be master over you — for you are not under Law, but under grace.
45_6_15: What then? Shall we sin because we are not under Law but under grace? May it never be!
45_6_16: Do you not know that when you present yourselves to someone as slaves for obedience, you are slaves of the one whom you obey — either of sin, resulting in death, or of obedience, resulting in righteousness?
45_6_17: But thanks be to God that though you were slaves of sin — you became obedient from the heart to that form of teaching to which you were committed.
45_6_18: And having been freed from sin, you became slaves of righteousness.
45_6_19: I am speaking in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh. For just as you presented your members as slaves to impurity and to lawlessness, resulting in further lawlessness — so now present your members as slaves to righteousness, resulting in sanctification.
45_6_20: For when you were slaves of sin, you were free in regard to righteousness.
45_6_21: Therefore what benefit were you then deriving from the things of which you are now ashamed? For the outcome of those things is death.
45_6_22: But now, having been freed from sin, and enslaved to God — you derive your benefit, resulting in sanctification, and the outcome, eternal life.
45_6_23: For the wages of sin is death — but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
45_7_1: Or do you not know, brothers (for I am speaking to those who know the law), that the law has jurisdiction over a person as long as he lives?
45_7_2: For the married woman is bound by law to her husband while he is living — but if her husband dies, she is released from the law concerning the husband.
45_7_3: So then, if while her husband is living she is joined to another man, she shall be called an adulteress. But if her husband dies, she is free from the law — so that she is not an adulteress, though she is joined to another man.
45_7_4: Therefore, my brothers, you also were made to die to the Law through the body of Christ — so that you might be joined to another, to Him who was raised from the dead, that we might bear fruit for God.
45_7_5: For while we were in the flesh, the sinful passions, which were aroused by the Law, were at work in the members of our body to bear fruit for death.
45_7_6: But now we have been released from the Law — having died to that by which we were bound — so that we serve in newness of the Spirit, and not in oldness of the letter.
45_7_7: What shall we say then? Is the Law sin? May it never be! On the contrary, I would not have come to know sin except through the Law. For I would not have known about coveting if the Law had not said, "You shall not covet."
45_7_8: But sin, taking opportunity through the commandment, produced in me coveting of every kind. For apart from the Law sin is dead.
45_7_9: I was once alive apart from the Law — but when the commandment came, sin became alive, and I died.
45_7_10: And this commandment — which was to result in life — proved to result in death for me.
45_7_11: For sin, taking an opportunity through the commandment, deceived me — and through it killed me.
45_7_12: So then, the Law is holy, and the commandment is holy and righteous and good.
45_7_13: Therefore did that which is good become a cause of death for me? May it never be! Rather it was sin — in order that it might be shown to be sin by effecting my death through that which is good — so that through the commandment sin would become utterly sinful.
45_7_14: For we know that the Law is spiritual — but I am of flesh, sold into bondage to sin.
45_7_15: For what I am doing, I do not understand. For I am not practicing what I would like to do — but I am doing the very thing I hate.
45_7_16: But if I do the very thing I do not want to do, I agree with the Law — confessing that the Law is good.
45_7_17: So now, no longer am I the one doing it — but sin which dwells in me.
45_7_18: For I know that nothing good dwells in me — that is, in my flesh. For the wishing is present in me — but the doing of the good is not.
45_7_19: For the good that I want, I do not do — but I practice the very evil that I do not want.
45_7_20: But if I am doing the very thing I do not want, I am no longer the one doing it — but sin which dwells in me.
45_7_21: I find then the principle that evil is present in me — the one who wants to do good.
45_7_22: For I joyfully concur with the law of God in the inner man.
45_7_23: But I see a different law in the members of my body — waging war against the law of my mind, and making me a prisoner of the law of sin which is in my members.
45_7_24: Wretched man that I am! Who will set me free from the body of this death?
45_7_25: Thanks be to God — through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, on the one hand I myself with my mind am serving the law of God — but on the other, with my flesh the law of sin.
45_8_1: Therefore there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
45_8_2: For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set you free from the law of sin and of death.
45_8_3: For what the Law could not do — weak as it was through the flesh — God did. Sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and as an offering for sin, He condemned sin in the flesh —
45_8_4: so that the requirement of the Law might be fulfilled in us, who do not walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.
45_8_5: For those who are according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh — but those who are according to the Spirit, the things of the Spirit.
45_8_6: For the mind set on the flesh is death — but the mind set on the Spirit is life and peace.
45_8_7: Because the mind set on the flesh is hostile toward God — for it does not subject itself to the law of God; for it is not even able to do so.
45_8_8: And those who are in the flesh cannot please God.
45_8_9: However, you are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit — if indeed the Spirit of God dwells in you. But if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to Him.
45_8_10: And if Christ is in you, though the body is dead because of sin — yet the spirit is alive because of righteousness.
45_8_11: But if the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you — He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit who dwells in you.
45_8_12: So then, brothers, we are under obligation — not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh.
45_8_13: For if you are living according to the flesh, you must die. But if by the Spirit you are putting to death the deeds of the body, you will live.
45_8_14: For all who are being led by the Spirit of God — these are sons of God.
45_8_15: For you have not received a spirit of slavery, leading to fear again — but you have received a spirit of adoption as sons, by which we cry out, "Abba! Father!"
45_8_16: The Spirit Himself testifies with our spirit that we are children of God.
45_8_17: And if children, then heirs also — heirs of God, and fellow heirs with Christ. If indeed we suffer with Him, so that we may also be glorified with Him.
45_8_18: For I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory that is to be revealed to us.
45_8_19: For the eager longing of the creation waits eagerly for the revealing of the sons of God.
45_8_20: For the creation was subjected to futility — not willingly, but because of Him who subjected it, in hope.
45_8_21: That the creation itself also will be set free from its slavery to corruption — into the freedom of the glory of the children of God.
45_8_22: For we know that the whole creation groans, and suffers the pains of childbirth together until now.
45_8_23: And not only this — but also we ourselves, having the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting eagerly for our adoption as sons — the redemption of our body.
45_8_24: For in hope we have been saved. But hope that is seen is not hope. For who hopes for what he already sees?
45_8_25: But if we hope for what we do not see, with perseverance we wait eagerly for it.
45_8_26: And in the same way the Spirit also helps our weakness. For we do not know how to pray as we should — but the Spirit Himself intercedes for us with groanings too deep for words.
45_8_27: And He who searches the hearts knows what the mind of the Spirit is — because He intercedes for the saints according to the will of God.
